content.text:
Agreed on the substance, with two modifications and one flag.

## Where I agree

Making `custom.md` point onward is better than what I proposed, for a reason I had missed: it means
**the pinned set needs to know nothing about `custom-family.md`**. The chain becomes
`AGENTS.md` -> `custom.md` -> `custom-family.md`, and four of the nine wiring points I listed
evaporate. AGENTS.md's hard rule 0, Terminology, File map, and the custom.md skeleton section all
stay as they are.

That also gives the right answer for a non-member: they get the payload's `custom.md`, the pointer
finds no file, and nothing dangles.

## Modification 1: the pointer is plumbing, not a convention

Putting it in `## Project conventions and overrides` makes all four members carry the same permanent
one-entry diff against the payload, over something none of us chose. It also reads as a divergence
when it is structure, and it costs us the claim we actually want to make, which is that our
conventions section is empty.

I would ship it in the payload's `custom.md` intro instead, worded so it is true whether or not the
file exists:

```markdown
# custom.md - <project>'s project layer

The project's own layer over the pinned agent-files (see
[AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md#custommd-the-project-layer)). Loaded last; on conflict, this file wins.

A project may carry a further layer: if `custom-family.md` is present beside this file, read it
too. It holds whatever this project's wider context requires and is absent when there is none.
```

Then `## Project conventions and overrides` is genuinely `_None._` for us, and no member diverges
from the payload over plumbing.

## Modification 2: the `@`-include is the load; the pointer is the documentation

A prose sentence is an instruction to a reader, not a load. Today `CLAUDE.md`'s `@custom.md` is what
actually puts the file in context. If the pointer is the only mechanism, a member who tidies
`custom.md` silently drops the whole family layer and nothing catches it.

So `CLAUDE.md` gets `@custom-family.md` as well. Belt and braces, costs one line, and the pointer
still earns its place by telling someone reading `custom.md` alone that a second layer exists.

## The proposed `custom-family.md`

Three sections, since you want the messaging documented there:

```markdown
# custom-family.md - <project>'s membership in the vc-x1 agent-file family

Read after [custom.md](custom.md). Present only in a member repo; a project that is not a member
does not carry this file.

## Membership

- **member name**: `<member>`
- **template repository**: `<path-to-template>`

## Messaging

Members leave word for each other in per-member mailboxes at the template repository; the protocol
is `<path-to-template>/MESSAGES.md` and it governs.

- **At acquaint, check `<path-to-template>/messages/<member>.md`**; an absent file means no mail.
- **Handle, then delete** the entry, and delete the file when it empties. Mailboxes hold open
  items only, so a message can never be a record: anything worth keeping goes to
  `notes/chores/chores-NN.md` before the entry is deleted.
- **Messages are thin pointers**, not state. Durable coordination state lives in topical files.

## Dogfood log

_None._

Dated entries on what this project is trying and where the pinned instructions chafed, failed, or
got amended; the evidence base for the family's convergence decisions (see
[Changing the agent-files](AGENTS.md#changing-the-agent-files)).

Each entry carries a **status**: `proposed` (in our agent-files, awaiting the family),
`adopted family-wide`, `rejected`, or `permanently local`. In-flight entries only: on resolution
an entry retires to `done.md` with its narrative in `notes/chores/chores-NN.md`, adopted and
rejected alike.
```

The handle-then-delete consequence is worth writing down there because we have already been bitten
by it: our 2026-08-05 convergence findings went into chores precisely because a deleted message
leaves no record, and that reasoning currently lives only in a dogfood bullet.

## The flag: this pulls a pinned rule back out of AGENTS.md

"Check the mailbox at acquaint" is a **pinned working practice** in the payload, added by vc-x1's
20260802 snapshot. Moving it to `custom-family.md` reverses a family decision, so it goes to vc-x1
as a proposal rather than as tidying. My argument for the reversal: a non-member cannot perform the
practice at all, since constructing the mailbox path needs a member name and a template path they do
not have, so it is not a harmless no-op for them, it is dead text naming concepts they lack.

There is a larger version of this question I would **not** open today. If the payload should be
usable by a non-member, then AGENTS.md's Terminology, hard rule 12, and "Changing the agent-files"
also talk about "the family" and "members" when the generic mechanism is really "the template
payload and my copy of it". That is a real inconsistency and I think we should name it to vc-x1 as
the next item rather than fold it in, because it would roughly double the review surface of a
configuration that is already large.

## Calls

1. **Pointer in the intro (my modification 1) or as the single conventions entry (your version)?**
   I recommend the intro.
2. **Does "Check the mailbox at acquaint" leave AGENTS.md**, or stay pinned and simply point at
   `custom-family.md` for the parameters? I recommend it leaves, and that we say so to vc-x1 as an
   explicit reversal.
3. **Do we raise the "AGENTS.md itself is family-flavored" question now or next?** I recommend next.

**The plain version:** your scheme is better than mine because it keeps the family out of the pinned
files entirely, so AGENTS.md needs no edits at all for this. I would put the pointer in `custom.md`'s
intro rather than in its conventions list, so we do not all carry an identical fake divergence, and
I would also add the `@`-include so the file actually loads rather than relying on prose. The one
thing that needs vc-x1's agreement rather than ours is pulling the mailbox practice back out of
AGENTS.md, since they pinned it five days ago.

# custom-family.md - iiac-perf's membership in the vc-x1 agent-file family

Read after [custom.md](custom.md), which points here. Present only in a member repo; a project
that is not a member does not carry this file, and nothing in it applies to one.

## Membership

- **member name**: `iiac-perf`
- **template repository**: `../vc-x1-template`

These two are environment rather than instruction, the same species as `.vc-config.toml`'s
`[repos]` paths, and they belong there instead. They cannot move yet: `vc-x1 config --validate`
rejects keys it does not know (measured on 0.78.4, 2026-08-07), so a config carrying them would
fail its own validator.

## Messaging

Members leave word for each other in per-member mailboxes at the template repository. The protocol
is `../vc-x1-template/MESSAGES.md` and it governs; these are the parts that decide how a session
behaves.

- **At acquaint, check `../vc-x1-template/messages/iiac-perf.md`**; an absent file means no mail.
- **Handle, then delete** the entry, and delete the file once it empties. Mailboxes hold open items
  only.
- **So a message can never be a record.** Anything in one worth keeping is copied into
  `notes/chores/chores-NN.md` *before* the entry is deleted. Learned 2026-08-05, when a
  convergence message carried measurements that would have been lost with it.
- **Messages are thin pointers, not state.** Durable coordination state lives in topical files; a
  message says "action needed, see <file>" rather than restating the details.
- **Write to a member's mailbox, never into their repo.** A repo with a live session is written
  only by its own agent.

## Dogfood log

Dated entries on what this project is trying and where the pinned instructions chafed, failed, or
got amended; the evidence base for the family's convergence decisions
([Changing the agent-files](AGENTS.md#changing-the-agent-files)).

Each entry carries a **status**: `proposed` (in our agent-files, awaiting the family),
`adopted family-wide`, `rejected`, or `permanently local`. In-flight entries only: on
resolution an entry retires to [done.md](notes/done.md) with its narrative in
`notes/chores/chores-NN.md`, adopted and rejected alike. Entries predating the status
convention keep their form until touched.

- 2026-08-07 (`proposed`): the family layer splits out of `custom.md`
  - `custom.md` had been accumulating things that only make sense because this repo belongs to a
    family: a member name, a template path, and a dogfood log whose status vocabulary reads
    `adopted family-wide`. wink's test is that `custom.md` should be usable as-is by a project that
    has never heard of us, and it failed that test
  - so the family layer moves here and `custom.md` keeps two sections, the medium and the project's
    own conventions. `custom.md`'s intro carries a conditional pointer at this file, which is what
    lets the pinned set stay ignorant of the split: the chain is `AGENTS.md` -> `custom.md` ->
    `custom-family.md`, and a non-member's pointer simply finds nothing
  - the pointer sits in the intro rather than in `## Project conventions and overrides`, so no
    member carries an identical one-entry diff against the payload over plumbing it did not choose
  - `CLAUDE.md` `@`-includes both files, because a prose pointer is documentation and not a load; a
    member who tidied `custom.md` would otherwise drop the whole family layer silently
  - one consequence needs the family's agreement, not ours: **"Check the mailbox at acquaint" leaves
    the pinned `AGENTS.md`** and lands in `## Messaging` above. vc-x1 pinned it in the 20260802
    snapshot, so this is a reversal. The argument is that a non-member cannot perform it at all,
    since building the mailbox path needs a member name and a template path they do not have, so it
    is dead text naming concepts they lack rather than a harmless no-op
  - deliberately not opened in the same pass: `AGENTS.md` still says "the family" and "member" where
    the generic mechanism is "the template payload and my copy of it". Same inconsistency one level
    up, and folding it in would roughly double the review surface of an already large configuration

- 2026-08-07 (`proposed`): cycles run on a bookmark, and `custom.md` stops holding rules
  - the bookmark rule had been adopted in principle since 2026-08-01 and was written down
    nowhere: `TODO.md` carried the intention, `cycle.md` said what a topic bookmark *is* once you
    have one, and neither creating nor landing one appeared in any agent-file. Two cycles ran on
    bookmarks anyway, on undocumented habit
  - so hard rule 13 states it, `cycle.md` gains an opening checklist and a land step, and
    `jj.md` gains the commands. Landing turns out to be the interesting half: it is the moment
    the cycle's commits become permanent, which makes it the trigger for the chores backfill
    that waits on permanence. That connection existed and had no owner
  - the create and land *commands* are deliberately separable from the rule, because wink
    expects a `vc-x1 start-change <bookmark>` to own the create half eventually
  - same pass, `custom.md` empties of conventions. Five entries were rules the family already
    has or should have, so they moved into the pinned files (two into `prose.md`, one into
    `versioning.md`, one into `AGENTS.md`) and two retired as answered
  - the sharpened convention behind it (wink): **intent decides the file, and nothing gates the
    edit**. A member writes a rule into its local pinned copy whenever it means the family to
    take it, without asking; `custom.md` is for what the member does *not* offer the family. The
    2026-08-05 entry below framed the same mechanism around experiments, which read as narrower
    than it is
  - cost, and it is the same one the 2026-08-05 entry recorded: our pinned files now hold more
    unreviewed text than before, and nothing at acquaint shows a reader which parts the family
    has agreed to. The diff is the answer and reading it is still manual

- 2026-08-06 (`permanently local`): pushes run from wink's shell, not the bot's sandboxed shell
  - `vc-x1 push` from the bot's sandboxed shell dies mid-transfer once the git stream is
    multi-MB (`send-pack: unexpected disconnect while reading sideband packet`), twice in a row
    on a roughly 3.4 MB bot-repo push
  - the identical command from wink's terminal succeeded first try, so the repos, keys, and
    remote are fine
  - **the cause is unknown, and it is not ssh** (corrected 2026-08-07). This entry first said the
    sandbox chokes the ssh stream at volume, inferred from a size correlation. Both remotes are
    and were `https://github.com/winksaville/...`, so the ssh explanation vc-x1 measured for its
    own identical-looking failures cannot be ours. The size correlation was the only evidence and
    it is not evidence
  - the workaround is unaffected: at push time the agent composes the command and asks wink to
    run it with the `!` prefix, which lands the output in the conversation, instead of invoking
    it in the sandbox
  - the failed runs also exposed a vc-x1 state bug (commit-work skipped, a transcript squashed
    into the wrong published bot commit); reported in the family mailbox 2026-08-06 and fixed by
    design at 0.78.x, which keeps no state and cannot resume
  - environment-bound so never family-wide; retire when a sandboxed push succeeds at volume. The
    next attempt is worth making blind, since 0.78.x changed the push transport under us

- 2026-08-05 (`proposed`): a step is a title; the version and the step number both leave the prose
  record
  - the version was a second identifier for a step, and any prose naming one could be invalidated
    by a history rewrite. This repo's 2026-08-01 renumber is the evidence: it left transcripts and
    pasted reports that only the decoder entry below can read
  - so the title becomes the identifier, a ladder rung carries neither a number nor a version, and
    the version-of-record is a build stamp living only in `Cargo.toml`. Every step still bumps it
  - the step number went too (wink): a rung sits in an ordered list, so a number beside it restates
    the position and then has to be maintained. Nothing renumbers, and a title need only be
    unambiguous within its cycle and within its chores file, where it is also an anchor
  - one exception, the chores as-built rung (wink): it records the version a *landed* commit
    carried, beside that commit's SHA, so the pair decodes an old `-V` banner. It takes the SHA's
    timing exactly, so an unlanded rung carries neither and a rebase cannot falsify a ladder
  - commit bodies tighten with it: a problem statement then a solution statement, both broad, with
    no file list, since the diff is already the mechanical record. The deliberation stays in
    chores, todo, and the session the `ochid:` trailer names, which is what the dual-repo model
    is for
  - that rule also took two passes. The first kept the body an edit list at one bullet per distinct
    change and survived one use, since writing this commit's own description produced thirteen
    bullets restating `git show --stat`. Clearing it exposed four contradictions of our own,
    including a title limit that read 50 in the authority file and 72 in three others
  - a topic bookmark is a draft until it lands, so keeping its ladder self-consistent may rewrite
    unlanded rungs; the exceptions are named rather than judged case by case
  - first cost measured, on this step itself: the version had been doubling as the eye's landmark
    in `## Done`, so removing it made the section hard to skim. `## Done` entries became a bold
    title plus sub-bullets, which is what `prose.md` had asked for all along and the version had
    been masking. We think other members will hit this wherever a long body hangs off a title in a
    flat list. Superseded in part 2026-08-07: vc-x1 wanted the version greppable, and the form is
    now the version ahead of the bold title, which serves both
  - drafted before the `measure-reproducibility` rebase so the cycle dogfoods it, per
    [Changing the agent-files](AGENTS.md#changing-the-agent-files); rationale in
    [chores-06](notes/chores/chores-06.md#docs-steps-are-titles-versions-are-stamps)

- 2026-08-05 (`proposed`): experiments move into the local agent-files, and `custom.md` narrows
  to what cannot be family-wide (superseded in scope by the 2026-08-07 entry above, which drops
  "experiment" for "anything the member offers the family")
  - the old rule sent every proposal to `custom.md` as an override, which made `custom.md` the
    staging area and guaranteed it grew non-generic, while the shared payload was the only place
    two members could collide
  - now the diff against the payload is the live proposal set and the commit history is the
    durable one, so neither has to be maintained by hand
  - the cost, recorded because it is real: a local agent-file no longer reads as family-agreed
    the way the payload does. We think an acquaint-time diff is the fix, and it is unbuilt
  - rationale in [chores-06](notes/chores/chores-06.md#docs-experiment-in-the-local-agent-files)
  - same session's family-convergence findings, kept in chores because the mailbox protocol is
    handle-then-delete, so a message can never be a record:
    - [jj revset primer audit](notes/chores/chores-06.md#jj-revset-primer-audit-2026-08-05): the
      payload's range bullets are wrong, and the error is the framing, not the gloss
    - [convergence measurements and positions](notes/chores/chores-06.md#convergence-measurements-and-positions-2026-08-05)

- 2026-08-02 (`proposed`): prose.md's <=100 wrap got misapplied as ~64 to match older files' look
  - the rule needed no change, the application did: surrounding narrow wrap is not a reason to
    wrap narrow, and one fact per sub-bullet beats a paragraph packing several (wink, reviewing
    TODO/chores additions)
  - extended to code comments at wink's direction
  - the application now lives in [prose.md](agent-data/prose.md#prose-form) itself, moved there
    2026-08-07; this entry stays until the family takes it

- 2026-08-01: published history renumbered under the new scope-based advancement rule
  - mapping: 0.24.0 -> 0.23.2 (grade-block compaction: presentation within the existing
    shape), 0.24.1 -> 0.23.3 (report docs), and the punctuation sweep lands as 0.23.4;
    0.24.0 stays reserved for the next architectural change
  - executed as a jj history rewrite of the two published commits (version-of-record and
    description; ochid trailers hand-copied per the re-describe rule) plus a force-push;
    safe because this repo has a single user and no external clones
  - permanent residue: bot-repo session transcripts and reports pasted in conversation carry
    the old `iiac-perf 0.24.0` / `0.24.1` banners; this mapping is the decoder
  - process finding: the rewrite would have been free had the cycles run on a topic bookmark
    landed onto `main` after review; "always work on a branch" added to TODO.md
- 2026-08-01: `vc-x1 push --body` rejects a body whose first character is `-`
  - a file-by-file body opening with its first bullet failed twice: once at vc-x1's own clap
    (worked around with `--body=`), then again inside push's `jj commit -m <body>` (same clap
    leading-hyphen rejection), which rolled both repos back cleanly
  - workaround that also satisfies prose form: open the body with its intro line, never a
    bare bullet
  - template finding: vc-x1 should pass bodies to jj as `-m=<body>` or via stdin/file

- 2026-07-31: adopted mid-dogfood-window
  - adoption base: the template's `AGENTS-vc-x1-f5-20260730-snapshot/` (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md,
    agent-data/), created the same day from vc-x1's live copy, the window's authority
  - local copies verified byte-identical to the snapshot at adoption (`diff -r`)
- 2026-07-31: adoption base amended before first commit
  - the snapshot's AGENTS.md gained rule 0 (read custom.md before acting) and hard-rules-first
    ordering; authored snapshot-side while vc-x1's session was live, with the pending sync to
    vc-x1 tracked in the template's snapshots.md
  - local AGENTS.md re-copied from the snapshot; pin set re-verified byte-identical
- 2026-07-31: template restructured into vc-x1-template; pin lines made generic
  - the template + coordination point is now the vc-x1-template repo: init payload in `work/`
    and `work.claude/`, discussion artifacts in `agents-protocol/`, mailboxes in `messages/`;
    the old vc-x1-work-repo-template and vc-x1-bot-repo-template are untouched pending wink's
    discussion with vc-x1
  - every "pinned to vc-x1-work-repo-template" line in the pin set became "the template
    repository" (snapshot-side amendment, same pending-sync flow as rule 0)
  - local pin set re-copied; snapshot, `work/`, and this repo verified three-way byte-identical
- 2026-07-31: first push under the new rules; two checklist gaps found (the 0.23.1 push)
  - given "desc and push", the agent jumped straight to the description: cycle.md's per-commit
    checklist has no step for backfilling the previous push's chores refs, bumping the
    version-of-record, or appending the chores record, so following it verbatim skips all
    three. Proposed template fix: add them as explicit steps before "write the description"
  - rule adopted (wink): **every commit belongs to a cycle, single- or multi-commit; there is
    no out-of-cycle push.** Mid-ladder the cycle is implied; otherwise ask "single- or
    multi-step cycle?" before preparing the commit. A single-commit cycle is a bare `X.Y.Z`
    close-out, so its validation is mandatory, and with no planning phase it skips
    `## In Progress` and goes straight to chores + Done
  - convention adopted (wink): chores commit references use the **as-built ladder form** for
    every cycle (rung `- [[N]] X.Y.Z[-n] <title>`), replacing the `Commits:` line; codified in
    agent-data/notes.md + cycle.md (snapshot-side, pending vc-x1 sync) and both
    cycle-protocol.md copies (this repo's and the template payload's); pre-existing
    `Commits:` lines are grandfathered
  - convention adopted (wink): chores files carry a **title-only `## Table of Contents`**, one
    `- [<title>](#<anchor>)` entry per commit-recording section; no versions or refs, so it
    never needs backfill (the TOC navigates, the ladder records); codified beside the ladder
    form, first instance in chores-05.md
- 2026-07-31: Todo #1 run as a single-commit cycle after a four-rung ladder was rejected
  - the proposed rungs split along implementation lines (print+parser / precision / README)
    and failed the test that makes a ladder worth having: no rung was independently valuable
    or revertable, and every intermediate state was a half-reshaped published report
  - refines the single-vs-multi question: multi-commit wants rungs that each stand alone;
    "one deliverable, several files" is single-commit shaped no matter how many edits it takes
- 2026-07-31: post-facto trapezoid experiment (0.23.0)
  - a published linear cycle was reshaped in place into the merge non-ff form with one
    `jj rebase -s` (close-out becomes the merge, rungs become the side leg, descendants
    follow); chids and ochid trailers survived, the bot repo needed nothing, and the one
    casualty was the close-out's recorded SHA, re-recorded per the backfill timing rule
  - details in chores-05.md "Post-facto trapezoid rewrite (2026-07-31)"; family-relevant if
    other repos want to adopt the trapezoid shape retroactively
  - the pre-restructure AGENTS.md is replaced (preserved in jj history, and verbatim as the
    template's AGENTS-iiac-perf.md)
  - the parked `punctuation-sweep` branch (TODO.md Todo #2) edited the old AGENTS.md; its
    AGENTS.md hunks are obsolete now that the typeable-punctuation rule ships as hard rule 8
    and prose.md, so the branch needs re-scoping to its README / TODO.md /
    notes/cycle-protocol.md conversions before landing
  - remaining pre-restructure local deltas (e.g. clap `verbatim_doc_comment` guidance) still
    need distilling into this file or proposing into the template; review findings recorded
    in the template's AGENTS-vc-x1-f5-20260730-review-iiac-perf-f5-20260731.md

# custom.md - iiac-perf's project layer

The project's own layer over the pinned agent-files (see
[AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md#custommd-the-project-layer)). Loaded last; on conflict, this file wins.

A project may carry a further layer: if `custom-family.md` is present beside this file, read it
too. It holds whatever this project's wider context requires and is absent when there is none.

## Medium and validation

The artifact is the `iiac-perf` CLI, a Rust crate (manifest `Cargo.toml`, package name
`iiac-perf`); versioning specifics in [versioning.md](notes/versioning.md).

**What a version bump promises**: nothing to a dependent, because there are none. `iiac-perf` is
a binary crate with no library target and no external consumers, so `X.Y.Z` is a scope signal to
readers of the history (see
[Advancing X.Y.Z](notes/versioning.md#advancing-xyz-scope-decides)) and not a compatibility
contract. Revisit with a compat clause if a library crate ever splits out.

- **Full validation**
  - when: per-commit checklist step 4; skip-able for notes-only commits, mandatory at close-out
  - run as separate invocations, each exit status checked:
    1. `cargo fmt`
    2. `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`
    3. `cargo test`
    4. `cargo install --path . --locked`
    5. (re-test if anything substantive changed)
- **Fast validation**
  - when: ladder checklist step 3
  - `cargo test --bins`

The commands are the project's; the rule that each invocation's exit status is checked is
universal and lives in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md#working-practices).

## Project conventions and overrides

_None._

Project-local conventions, and overrides of the pinned files; an override names the section it
supersedes.

[custom.md](custom.md) is an agent-file like the others, and the aim is that it stays as generic
as they do. The family's goal is a byte-identical pinned set, so custom.md holds only what a
pinned file structurally cannot.

**Its skeleton is family-wide even though its content cannot be.** custom.md is the one agent-file
that is never pinned, since every project's content differs by construction. What converges is the
section set: these four `##` headers, in this order, each meaning the same thing everywhere. A
member's file is the payload's skeleton with the angle brackets filled in, so a diff against the
payload shows substitutions and no structure. The sections:

- **`## Medium and validation`**: the medium and its validation commands (what the per-commit
  checklist's "validate the artifact" runs), what a version bump promises this artifact's users,
  and versioning specifics beyond [versioning.md](notes/versioning.md). Not a divergence and not
  negotiable, since another medium could not adopt them if it wanted to.
- **`## Community identity`**: the per-checkout facts the pinned mailbox practice points at, this
  project's member name and the template repository's path. Environment rather than instruction,
  and headed for `.vc-config.toml` once its schema carries them.
- **`## Local rules`**: a rule the project means to keep without offering it to the family. Each
  entry names the pinned section it supersedes and says **why it cannot be family-wide**.
- **`## Dogfood log`**: dated entries on what this project is trying and where the instructions
  chafed, each carrying a status. In-flight entries only; resolved ones retire.

The last two are **empty at birth**, and `## Local rules` should usually stay that way. A rule the
project would keep and another member might not is still a *proposal* until the family rejects it,
so by default it belongs in the pinned file where the rule lives (see
[Changing the agent-files](#changing-the-agent-files)), where it shows up as a diff the family
reviews. Writing it into custom.md instead hides it from exactly the review that should decide it,
which is why an entry has to justify itself. Environment-bound facts are the clear-cut case:
another member could not adopt them if it wanted to. An empty section stays, with `_None._` under
it, so the skeleton is one shape rather than a shape per member.

Precedence: custom.md is loaded last and wins conflicts with this file and the satellites.

input.content:
### The family layer splits out of `custom.md`, which is a shape proposal rather than a rule one

wink diffed our `custom.md` against `work/custom.md` and the two files do not even begin the same.
Chasing that produced a sharper test than "do the sections match", and `custom.md` failed it:
**`work/custom.md` should be usable as-is by a project that has never heard of us.** Today it is
not. It carries a member name, a template path, and a `## Project conventions and overrides`
section whose real subject is what a member owes the family. Our own copy was worse, with a dogfood
log whose status vocabulary reads `adopted family-wide`.

So the family layer moves into a new **`custom-family.md`**, and the pinned set learns nothing about
it. The chain is `AGENTS.md` -> `custom.md` -> whatever `custom.md` points at, and a non-member's
pointer finds nothing. Concretely, `AGENTS.md` needs no knowledge of the new file at all: its hard
rule 0, Terminology and File map say "and the further layer custom.md points at", never a filename.

**Proposed `work/custom.md`**, two sections, no family anywhere in it:

```markdown
# custom.md - <project>'s project layer

The project's own layer over the pinned agent-files (see
[AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md#custommd-the-project-layer)). Loaded last; on conflict, this file wins.

A project may carry a further layer: if `custom-family.md` is present beside this file, read it
too. It holds whatever this project's wider context requires and is absent when there is none.

## Medium and validation

<what the artifact is; manifest and package name; see agent-data/versioning.md>

**What a version bump promises**: <what X.Y.Z commits this artifact to for its users, or that it
commits nothing because it has none; see
[Advancing X.Y.Z](agent-data/versioning.md#advancing-xyz-scope-decides)>

- **Full validation**
  - when: per-commit checklist step 5; skip-able for notes-only commits, mandatory at close-out
  - <the medium's commands, run as separate invocations, each exit status checked>
- **Fast validation**
  - when: ladder checklist step 3
  - <the medium's quick check>

The commands are the project's; the rule that each invocation's exit status is checked is
universal and lives in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md#working-practices).

## Project conventions and overrides

_None._

Project-local conventions, and overrides of the pinned files; an override names the section it
supersedes.
```

**Proposed `work/custom-family.md`**, shipped in the payload for members to fill in:

```markdown
# custom-family.md - <project>'s membership in the vc-x1 agent-file family

Read after [custom.md](custom.md), which points here. Present only in a member repo; a project
that is not a member does not carry this file, and nothing in it applies to one.

## Membership

- **member name**: `<member>`
- **template repository**: `<path-to-template>`

## Messaging

Members leave word for each other in per-member mailboxes at the template repository. The protocol
is `<path-to-template>/MESSAGES.md` and it governs; these are the parts that decide how a session
behaves.

- **At acquaint, check `<path-to-template>/messages/<member>.md`**; an absent file means no mail.
- **Handle, then delete** the entry, and delete the file once it empties. Mailboxes hold open items
  only.
- **So a message can never be a record.** Anything in one worth keeping is copied into
  `notes/chores/chores-NN.md` *before* the entry is deleted.
- **Messages are thin pointers, not state.** Durable coordination state lives in topical files.
- **Write to a member's mailbox, never into their repo.** A repo with a live session is written
  only by its own agent.

## Dogfood log

_None._

Dated entries on what this project is trying and where the pinned instructions chafed, failed, or
got amended; the evidence base for the family's convergence decisions
([Changing the agent-files](AGENTS.md#changing-the-agent-files)).

Each entry carries a **status**: `proposed` (in our agent-files, awaiting the family),
`adopted family-wide`, `rejected`, or `permanently local`. In-flight entries only: on resolution
an entry retires to `done.md` with its narrative in `notes/chores/chores-NN.md`, adopted and
rejected alike.
```

Three details worth your eye, because each was a decision rather than a transcription:

- **The pointer is in `custom.md`'s intro, not in its conventions list.** Making it a conventions
  entry would have every member carrying an identical one-entry diff against the payload over
  plumbing none of us chose, and it would read as a divergence when it is structure. In the intro,
  our conventions section is genuinely `_None._`, which is the claim we actually want to make.
- **`CLAUDE.md` `@`-includes both files.** A prose pointer documents; only an import loads. If the
  pointer were the sole mechanism, a member tidying `custom.md` would drop the entire family layer
  and nothing would catch it.
- **`_None._` under an empty section rather than omitting the section**, so the skeleton is one
  shape everywhere and a reader can tell "nothing here" from "this member never adopted it".

**One item in this needs your agreement rather than ours, and it is a reversal.** "Check the mailbox
at acquaint" is a pinned working practice you added in the 20260802 snapshot, and the split takes it
out of `AGENTS.md` and into `custom-family.md`'s `## Messaging`. Our argument: a non-member cannot
perform it at all, since building the mailbox path needs a member name and a template path they do
not have, so it is not a harmless no-op for them but dead text naming concepts they lack. If you
would rather it stay pinned and merely point at the further layer for its parameters, say so and we
will put it back.

**And one we deliberately did not open.** The same test applied to `AGENTS.md` would find plenty:
Terminology, hard rule 12 and "Changing the agent-files" all say "the family" and "member" where the
generic mechanism is "the template payload and my copy of it". We think that is a real
inconsistency and the natural next item, but folding it into this configuration would roughly double
its review surface, so we are naming it rather than acting on it.

### What else is in the diff

Beyond your six, so your review knows the whole shape:

- **Cycles run on a bookmark**, which had been adopted in principle here since 2026-08-01 and
  written down nowhere. New hard rule 13, a `cycle.md` section, an Opening checklist, a land step in
  the Close-out checklist, and the commands in `jj.md` under "Cycle bookmarks: create and land".
  Landing turned out to be the interesting half: it is when a cycle's commits become permanent, so
  it is the trigger for the chores backfill that waits on permanence, a connection that existed and
  had no owner. The rule and the commands are deliberately separable, since wink expects a
  `vc-x1 start-change <bookmark>` to own the create half eventually.
- **Long-lived bookmarks: merge-only by default, deletable once merged**, adopted from your payload
  verbatim in substance, sited next to the cycle-bookmark rule so the contrast is visible: a cycle
  bookmark is a draft and may be rewritten, a long-lived one is published and may not.
- **Hard rule 12 reframed** to wink's sharper statement: *intent decides where a rule change is
  written, and nothing gates the edit*. A member writes a rule into its local pinned copy whenever
  it means the family to take it, without asking first; the review happens at convergence, on the
  diff. This subsumes our 2026-08-05 "experiment locally" framing, which read as narrower than it
  was.

  moved into the pinned files: write-to-the-full-width and cycle-bookend-titles into `prose.md`
  (adopting your payload's wording, which shrinks our diff), the mailbox practice into `AGENTS.md`,
  scope-based version advancement into `versioning.md` as a new "Advancing X.Y.Z: scope decides".
  Two retired as answered: the `--scope` rename note (0.78.4 has no `--scope` on push at all) and

- **`custom.md`'s categories**, in AGENTS.md: medium-determined, community identity, rules the
  project does not offer the family, and the dogfood log. The third should usually be empty and has
  to justify itself; ours is empty, which is the claim this change is really making.

```markdown
# custom.md - iiac-perf's project layer

The project's own layer over the pinned agent-files (see AGENTS.md#custommd-the-project-layer).
Loaded last; on conflict, this file wins.

A project may carry a further layer: if `custom-family.md` is present beside this file, read it
too. It holds whatever this project's wider context requires and is absent when there is none.

## Medium and validation
   ... Rust/cargo, and what a version bump promises

## Project conventions and overrides

_None._
```

The pointer is in the intro, so our conventions section is genuinely empty rather than carrying a
one-entry fake divergence.

## `custom-family.md` — Membership, Messaging, Dogfood log

`## Messaging` now writes down the mailbox rules that were scattered: check at acquaint,
handle-then-delete, **so a message can never be a record** (copy anything worth keeping into chores
first), thin pointers not state, and write to a mailbox rather than into another member's repo. That
third one had been living only as a dogfood bullet even though it is the rule that saved our
2026-08-05 convergence measurements.

The log gained a new entry recording the split, including the two things that need vc-x1 rather than
us.

## What this bought in the pinned set

`AGENTS.md` now never names `custom-family.md`. Hard rule 0, Terminology, and the File map all say
"the further layer `custom.md` points at", so the chain extends without the pinned set knowing what
is at the end of it. Its `custom.md` section is back to a two-header skeleton.

**"Check the mailbox at acquaint" is gone from `AGENTS.md`'s working practices** and lives in
`## Messaging`. That is the reversal of vc-x1's 20260802 pin, flagged as such in the message and in
the dogfood log rather than slipped in.

`CLAUDE.md` imports both files. The pointer documents; the import loads.

## Also updated

`agent-data/notes.md`'s "Retiring Done entries" no longer names `custom.md` as the dogfood log's
home — it says "wherever the project keeps its log", which is the same family-agnostic move.
`TODO.md` #4's description of what survives in `custom.md` was corrected.

The queued message to vc-x1 had its single-file skeleton section replaced with the two-file
proposal, both skeletons pasted verbatim, the three decisions explained (pointer in the intro, the
`@`-include, `_None._` over omission), the mailbox reversal called out as needing their agreement,
and the `AGENTS.md`-is-also-family-flavored question named as the next item rather than folded in.
Two stale bullets elsewhere in the message were fixed to match.

Checks: anchors clean in both new files (same 19 pre-existing breakages elsewhere, none mine), no
over-width lines except unbreakable link atoms. Nothing committed or pushed; `custom-family.md`
shows as `A` in the working copy.

1	# Notes file conventions
2	
3	Conventions the bot follows when reading and writing notes files (`TODO.md`,
4	`notes/todo-backlog.md`, `notes/bugs.md`, `notes/chores/chores-NN.md`, `notes/done.md`). One
5	source of truth lives here; [`notes/README.md`](../notes/README.md) points back. Read this
6	before editing a notes file.
7	
8	Universal file, shared with the template repository; a proposed change is edited here and
9	converges at the template ([Changing the agent-files](../AGENTS.md#changing-the-agent-files)).
10	Project-local content goes in the [project layer](../AGENTS.md#terminology).
11	
12	## File reads: read the slice you need
13	
14	Long notes files are appended to over time. Read only the slice your task needs; grep or read
15	further on demand.
16	
17	- **`TODO.md`** (the routine acquaint read): the first ~60 lines covers intro + `## In
18	  Progress` + the top of the ranked `## Todo` (priorities, #1 highest). `Read` with
19	  `offset=0, limit=60`. `## Ideas` sits below `## Todo`; read further only when chasing a
20	  lower-ranked entry, an Idea, a `[N]` ref, or auditing the whole list.
21	- **`notes/todo-backlog.md`**: the long-tail backlog (lower-priority entries below the ranked
22	  `## Todo`). Read only when picking up a backlog item; grep to locate it first.
23	- **`notes/bugs.md`**: the bug list. Small; read whole when triaging a bug or chasing the
24	  `## Bugs` pointer in TODO.md.
25	- **`notes/done.md`** + **`notes/chores/chores-NN.md`**: historical / append-mostly. Scan
26	  headings first (`grep '^## ' notes/chores/chores-NN.md`), then read only the section you
27	  need.
28	
29	**Why:** the routine read should stay small. `TODO.md` grows every cycle, so the backlog and
30	bugs live in files under `notes/` rather than inline; the same "slice you need" rule applies
31	to historical files.
32	
33	## Notes references
34	
35	Reference *citations* are double-bracketed so the brackets render: `[[N]]`, or `[[2]],[[3]]`
36	for several (comma-separated, not `[2,3]` or `[[2]][[3]]`). The `[N]:` definitions in a file's
37	`# References` section and inline `[text](url)` / `[text](#anchor)` links stay
38	single-bracketed.
39	
40	## Reference numbering
41	
42	Every note file (`TODO.md`, `todo-backlog.md`, `bugs.md`, `chores-NN.md`, `done.md`) keeps a
43	file-local `# References` section at the bottom. Reference numbers are scoped to that file:
44	`[1]` in `chores-07.md` and `[1]` in `chores-01.md` are independent slots that may point at
45	completely different URLs. New chores files start their numbering at `[1]`.
46	
47	Treat `[N]` like a **footnote**: the number is a local slot, only meaningful within its file's
48	`# References`. So a `[N]` *citation* (bare `[N]`, or doubled `[[N]]`) never reuses another
49	file's number; to cite a target a sibling file references, pick your own next-local slot and
50	define it (the same target may carry a different number in each file). A `[N]` *inside a code
51	span* (`` `[72]` ``) is different: that's a quoted identifier, literal text naming a ref-key
52	(often from another file's namespace), data, not a citation; it needs no definition here. To
53	point at a section of another file from prose, use an inline link with an anchor,
54	`[that section](../chores-07.md#...)`, not a bare number.
55	
56	A `chores-NN.md` `# References` entry is usually a `/notes/<file>.md#anchor` (or
57	`/ARCHITECTURE.md`) path, but may also be a **commit reference**,
58	`[N]: <commit-url-with-12-hex-SHA> "<full-40-hex-SHA>"`, cited by a rung of a section's
59	as-built ladder. See [Chores commit references](#chores-commit-references) for the why and the
60	exact shape.
61	
62	A file's `# References` can be **re-packed** to a contiguous `[1]..[N]` in
63	first-citation-appearance order: walk the file's prose in document order (`TODO.md`: `## Todo`
64	then `## Done`; `chores-NN.md`: top to bottom) and number refs as their first `[[N]]` citation
65	appears. This is a file-local rewrite, so only that file's `[[N]]` citations and `[N]:`
66	definitions move; every target and sibling file is untouched. A `[[N]]` inside a `` ` `` code
67	span is a literal token, not a citation, and is left alone. Do it opportunistically (when the
68	namespace has drifted enough to annoy), not on a schedule: `TODO.md` fragments fastest (entries
69	land and get pruned every cycle) and is the usual candidate; `chores-NN.md` / `done.md` are
70	append-mostly and only need it after an unusual event (e.g. a bulk retrofit that allocated
71	slots out of document order).
72	
73	## Markdown anchor links
74	
75	GitHub anchor algorithm: lowercase, strip non-alphanumeric characters in place, map remaining
76	spaces to hyphens 1-for-1. Do **not** collapse adjacent whitespace, so `a + b` -> `a--b`
77	(spaces on both sides of `+`), but `a: b` -> `a-b` (only trailing space on `:`). General
78	markdown reference: [markdownguide.org](https://www.markdownguide.org). GitHub publishes no
79	official spec for auto-generated anchors; the de-facto reference implementation is
80	[github-slugger](https://github.com/Flet/github-slugger).
81	
82	## Todo format
83	
84	`TODO.md` is organized into `## In Progress`, `## Todo` (strict priority rank, #1 highest;
85	long-tail backlog in [todo-backlog.md](../notes/todo-backlog.md)), `## Ideas`, `## Bugs`
86	(pointer to [bugs.md](../notes/bugs.md)), and `## Done` sections. Each item is a short
87	description with reference links to more detail.
88	
89	`## Todo` and `## Bugs` entries carry explicit `1.` `2.` ... numbers in the source. For
90	`## Todo` the number is its **priority rank** (#1 highest, descending); for `## Bugs` it's just
91	an index. They're for grepping and at-a-glance "let's do #1", **not stable IDs**: reorder (to
92	reprioritize), insert, or delete freely, then `vc-x1 fix-todo --no-dry-run` renumbers and
93	normalizes continuation-line indent, so any given number is positional. **To refer to a Todo
94	durably, name it by its title, a plain, greppable text mention.** Not its number (positional,
95	renumbered) and not a markdown link: a numbered list item has no anchor to link to.
96	
97	Numbering helps a human orient in a long list but makes links difficult and fragile, especially
98	an external reference pointing in, which can't be auto-fixed when the list renumbers. A robust
99	fix (a number-free anchor, or a number-tolerant dereference that matches the title slug and
100	wildcards the numeric prefix, since a GitHub slug like `5-foo` is encoded, not opaque, so the
101	title is recoverable) is a `validate-numbering` design question, out of scope here.
102	
103	`vc-x1 fix-todo` alone only previews; `vc-x1 validate-todo` is the read-only check. The
104	`## Done` section keeps `-` bullets, since items aren't referenced by number once completed.
105	
106	Example shape:
107	
108	```
109	# Todo
110	1. Add new feature X [details](features.md#feature-x)
111	2. Fix bug Y [[1]]
112	
113	# Done
114	- **Fixed issue Z** [[2]],[[3]]
115	
116	[1]: bugs.md#bug-y
117	[2]: issues.md#issue-z
118	[3]: fixes.md#fix-z
119	```
120	
121	## Done entry form
122	
123	A `## Done` entry (in `TODO.md` and in `done.md`) is the close-out's **version**, then a **bold
124	title line** carrying its chores `[[N]]` ref, with any detail as sub-bullets:
125	
126	```
127	- 0.42.0 **feat: config loader** [[7]]
128	  - `--config` resolves per-profile pin pools
129	  - the parse rejects unknown keys rather than ignoring them
130	```
131	
132	- **Bold, and detail below rather than beside.** These entries are read by skimming a list for
133	  one of them, so the title has to be findable without reading the line it sits on. A title
134	  followed by a paragraph of summary is the wall-of-prose shape
135	  [Prose form](prose.md#prose-form) warns about, and it hides the one thing a skim is looking
136	  for. Bold matches the `## In Progress` block, whose title line is already bold.
137	- **The version leads and the title stays bold**, so the entry answers both questions a reader
138	  brings: `grep 0.42.0` finds what shipped in a version, and the eye still lands on titles when

1	# Versioning
2	
3	How this project versions its commits and the running artifact. The scheme, meaning the manifest's
4	suffix spelling and the unique-per-commit aim, is generic and shared across projects: this file is
5	copied **verbatim**, with
6	[Recording the version-of-record](#recording-the-version-of-record) covering each medium by
7	conditional rather than per-project edits.
8	
9	## Terms
10	
11	Three names, used as defined here across
12	[AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md),
13	[cycle-protocol.md](cycle-protocol.md), and the notes files:
14	
15	- **version**: the per-commit version (e.g. `0.3.0-5.3.0`). It lives in the manifest. No
16	  ladder, todo entry, commit title, or commit body writes one, the one exception being the
17	  chores as-built rung recording a landed commit (see
18	  [Versions live in the version-of-record only](../agent-data/prose.md#versions-live-in-the-version-of-record-only)),
19	  and its suffix encodes the cycle phase for whoever inspects the manifest (see
20	  [Suffix scheme](#suffix-scheme)).
21	- **version-of-record**: the authoritative stored copy of the version, in the project's manifest
22	  (see [Recording the version-of-record](#recording-the-version-of-record)); a built or running
23	  artifact derives from it.
24	- **versioning**: the topic, this scheme as a whole.
25	
26	## A stamp, not a name
27	
28	The version answers "which commit produced this artifact". It is not a name for a step: a step is
29	named by its title and located by its position in the ladder list (see
30	[Steps are named, not numbered](../agent-data/prose.md#steps-are-named-not-numbered)). So the
31	suffix below is the only number in the system, and since nothing dereferences it, reordering or
32	inserting a step leaves the versions already committed alone.
33	
34	## Advancing X.Y.Z: scope decides
35	
36	Which of the three numbers moves is decided by the **scope of the change**, not by whether it
37	touched code: **minor for architecture, patch for everything else.**
38	
39	- The test is whether the *shape* of the system changed or only its contents. Minor when the
40	  structure moves: a subsystem added or removed, a pipeline reshaped, an output contract
41	  redesigned. Patch for work within the existing shape: incremental features, new cases,
42	  presentation, docs, notes.
43	- **A docs-only change can be a minor** and a large code change can be a patch. Volume is not
44	  scope, and the earlier functional-versus-docs test kept getting this backwards.
45	- **Major is a project's own call**, since what `X` promises depends on the artifact and its
46	  users; the project records that promise in its
47	  [project layer](../AGENTS.md#terminology).
48	
49	**Why:** the suffix already encodes a commit's phase, so `X.Y.Z` is free to encode the only other
50	thing a reader wants from a version at a glance, how big a change they are looking at.
51	
52	## Recording the version-of-record
53	
54	Where the version-of-record lives, how it's stored and surfaced, and how often it changes. Pick
55	the case that fits your medium:
56	
57	- **Manifest**, where the version-of-record is stored:
58	  - if Rust, `Cargo.toml` `[package].version`
59	  - if Python, `pyproject.toml` `[project].version` (or the committed config it's sourced from)
60	  - otherwise wherever the medium records it (a generic `version.toml`, a book's frontmatter,
61	    ...); add the case as needed
62	- **Notation**, how the `-` form is stored:
63	  - if the format allows `-` (TOML `version.toml`, `Cargo.toml`), store it verbatim
64	  - if it bars `-` (PEP 440's local segment, e.g. a Python project), remap to `+`, so
65	    `0.3.0-5.3.0` becomes `0.3.0+5.3.0`: same version, just the stored spelling
66	- **Reporter**, how a built artifact surfaces the version-of-record:
67	  - if a CLI app, `<cli-app> -V`
68	  - if a TUI/GUI, add to Help/About or display on the title
69	- **Cadence**, how often to bump: see
70	  [Unique per commit](#unique-per-commit-preference-not-requirement); this project follows the
71	  per-commit preference.
72	
73	## Unique per commit (preference, not requirement)
74	
75	Our general notion is that the version-of-record should change on **every commit**, so a built or
76	running artifact identifies the exact commit it came from.
77	
78	- This is a preference, **not** a hard requirement. A project following the cycle protocol may
79	  bump less often: once per cycle, only at release, and so on. Record the choice in
80	  [Recording the version-of-record](#recording-the-version-of-record) if it differs.
81	- It is achievable because the cycle's versions (below) are **pre-assignable**, unlike the git
82	  SHA, which a commit cannot contain (see the cycle protocol's
83	  [Commits backfill](cycle-protocol.md#commits-backfill)).
84	
85	## Suffix scheme
86	
87	The cycle (Preparation -> Work -> Close-out; see [cycle-protocol.md](cycle-protocol.md)) encodes
88	each commit's phase in the version suffix, the **final identifier `0` marking a Preparation**.
89	
90	This is the manifest's own spelling, read by whoever inspects `Cargo.toml` or `-V` output. It is
91	not a name for a step: a step is identified by its title, and an in-flight ladder rung carries
92	neither a number nor a version (see
93	[Steps are named, not numbered](../agent-data/prose.md#steps-are-named-not-numbered)). The one
94	prose surface that records a version is a chores as-built rung, where it is a property of a landed
95	commit sitting beside that commit's SHA. The identifiers below count commits within a phase;
96	nothing dereferences one.
97	
98	- `X.Y.Z-0`: Preparation
99	- `X.Y.Z-1`, `X.Y.Z-2`, ...: Work commits
100	- `X.Y.Z`: Close-out (bare version, no suffix)
101	
102	**Preparation is optional.** A lightweight cycle, with no ladder and no setup commit, skips `-0`
103	and starts at `-1` (its first Work commit). The same holds at every level: a sub-cycle needing no
104	Preparation omits its `.0` (see Nesting). One that grows a Preparation later adds the `0` step
105	without renumbering siblings.
106	
107	Disambiguation:
108	
109	- `-10`: Work commit #10 (final identifier `10`), not a Preparation.
110	- `-1.0`: Preparation of the `-1` sub-cycle (final identifier `0`).
111	
112	**Nesting.** Sub-cycles append another level, recursively:
113	
114	- `X.Y.Z-3.0`: Preparation of the `-3` sub-cycle
115	- `X.Y.Z-3.1`, `X.Y.Z-3.2`: its Work
116	- `X.Y.Z-3`: its Close-out
117	- `X.Y.Z-3.1.0`: Preparation of the `-3.1` sub-sub-cycle
118	
119	Bump the version-of-record at the start of each phase, so the active phase is recorded and, per
120	the preference above, every commit carries a distinct version.

1	# jj and cross-repo linking
2	
3	How version control is driven on this project (jj, never raw git) and how the two repos'
4	commits point at each other (the `ochid:` trailer). Read this before any jj operation beyond
5	`st` / `log` / `diff`, and always before touching a commit description.
6	
7	Universal file, shared with the template repository; a proposed change is edited here and
8	converges at the template ([Changing the agent-files](../AGENTS.md#changing-the-agent-files)).
9	Project-local content goes in the [project layer](../AGENTS.md#terminology).
10	
11	## jj Basics
12	
13	**Use jj, not git, for version-control operations** (status, log, diff, commit, push, history
14	rewrite). jj coexists with the git backend, so the repo *can* be driven with raw `git`, but
15	this project's workflow (bookmarks, the working-copy `@` model, ochid trailers) is expressed in
16	jj terms; reaching for `git` invites state that doesn't match the jj documentation here. There
17	is no `jj mv`: to move/rename a tracked file, just `mv` it on disk and jj detects the rename by
18	content.
19	
20	- `jj st -R .` / `jj st -R .claude`: show working copy status
21	- `jj log -R .` / `jj log -R .claude`: show commit log
22	- `jj commit -m "title" -m "body" -R <repo>`: finalize working copy into a commit
23	- `jj describe -m "title" -m "body" -R <repo>`: set description without committing
24	- `jj git push --bookmark <name> -R <repo>`: push a bookmark (no `--allow-new` flag; jj pushes
25	  new bookmarks without special flags)
26	- `jj bookmark set <name> -r <rev> -R <repo>`: create the bookmark, or move an existing one, at
27	  `<rev>`. Moving it backwards needs `--allow-backwards`
28	- `jj git push --named <name>=<rev> -R <repo>`: create *and* publish in one step, which is the
29	  usual way a cycle's bookmark is born (see [Cycle bookmarks](#cycle-bookmarks-create-and-land))
30	- In jj, the working copy (@) is always a mutable commit being edited. `jj commit` finalizes it
31	  and creates a new empty working copy on top.
32	- The bot repo always has uncommitted changes during an active session because session data
33	  updates continuously.
34	- `jj rebase` uses `--onto`/`-o` to name the destination(s).
35	
36	## Cross-repo linking (ochid trailers)
37	
38	The cross-reference between the work repo and the bot repo is what makes the dual-repo work:
39	every commit points at its counterpart in the other repo, so the "what" (code) and the
40	"why / how" (session) stay linked across time. That pointer is the **ochid** (Other Change ID)
41	git trailer.
42	
43	A **chid** is jj's change ID, a permanent identifier that survives rebases and `describe`s
44	(unlike the commit ID / git SHA, which changes on rewrite). An **ochid** trailer carries the
45	counterpart commit's chid as a workspace-root-relative path:
46	
47	- Paths start with `/`, the workspace root, i.e. the work repo (the project root). `/.claude`
48	  is the bot sub-repo.
49	- `ochid: /<chid>` references a change in the **work repo**.
50	- `ochid: /.claude/<chid>` references a change in the **bot repo**.
51	
52	Trailers are blank-line-separated `key: value` lines at the end of the commit body, using the
53	chid's **12-character** prefix:
54	
55	```
56	ochid: /.claude/xvzvruqowktp   # points to a bot-repo change
57	ochid: /wtpmottvxqzl           # points to a work-repo change
58	```
59	
60	How many, and which direction:
61	
62	- **Work-repo commits** each carry one `ochid: /.claude/<bot-chid>`, the bot repo's change ID.
63	- **The bot-repo commit** carries one `ochid: /<work-chid>` per work-repo commit in that push.
64	  The count is per *push*, not per cycle. A trapezoid close-out whose rungs were pushed 1:1 as
65	  they landed still carries exactly one; more than one occurs when a single push publishes
66	  several work-repo commits.
67	
68	Use `vc-x1 chid -s work,bot -L` to capture the change IDs (first line work repo, second bot
69	repo).
70	
71	`ochid:` trailers are **stamped by `vc-x1 push`**; never hand-write them into a commit body or
72	`--title`/`--body`.
73	
74	## Re-describing: coordinate first, and keep the trailer
75	
76	**Never `jj describe` a commit that is already published or already carries trailers without
77	coordinating with everyone involved first.** It is a history rewrite, and it silently drops the
78	cross-repo link. Describing a fresh local commit that has never been described and carries no
79	trailers is authoring a message rather than rewriting one, and is not covered; that is the
80	sub-cycle ladder's
81	[per-Work-commit contract](../notes/cycle-protocol.md#per-work-commit-contract-within-a-ladder)
82	step 4.
83	
84	When a re-describe is agreed, copy any `ochid:` trailers into the new body by hand (the "don't
85	hand-write trailers" rule covers push authoring a message from scratch, not preserving one
86	already stamped). Hit at the 0.77.2 amend (2026-07-29), where the trailer survived only that
87	way; `vc-x1 fix-desc` repairs a dropped one by title match.
88	
89	## Cycle bookmarks: create and land
90	
91	The mechanics behind [Cycles run on a bookmark](cycle.md#cycles-run-on-a-bookmark); that section
92	holds the rule and when it applies, this one holds the commands.
93	
94	**Create**, at the cycle's opening, with the bookmark named for the cycle rather than the step:
95	
96	- `jj git push --named <bookmark>=@- -R .` is the common case: it creates the bookmark at the
97	  last committed change and publishes it in one invocation.
98	- Any other revision works as the `=<rev>` right-hand side. When `<rev>` is not `@-`, follow with
99	  `jj new <rev> -R .` so the working copy actually sits on the new line; otherwise the bookmark
100	  exists and the next commit lands somewhere else.
101	- `jj bookmark set <bookmark> -r <rev> -R .` creates it without publishing, for a line that is
102	  not ready to be seen.
103	
104	**Land**, once the close-out is approved: fast-forward the permanent branch to the bookmark.
105	
106	- `jj bookmark set main -r <bookmark> -R .`, then `jj git push --bookmark main -R .`.
107	- It is a fast-forward, so `--allow-backwards` is not wanted; needing it means the bookmark is
108	  not a descendant of `main` and the situation wants a look, not a flag.
109	- Landing is the moment the cycle's commits become permanent, so it triggers the records that
110	  wait on permanence: the chores as-built rungs take their SHAs and versions
111	  ([Chores commit references](notes.md#chores-commit-references)).
112	- The bookmark is redundant once landed and may be deleted (`jj bookmark delete <bookmark>`),
113	  the same disposal the long-lived case gets below.
114	
115	We think a `vc-x1 start-change <bookmark>` will eventually own the create half; it would replace
116	the create bullets and nothing else, which is why the rule and the commands are separated.
117	
118	## Long-lived bookmarks: merge-only by default, deletable once merged
119	
120	A long-lived bookmark (a program line pushed rung by rung across cycles) is not a cycle bookmark:
121	it carries published history, and the discipline protects that history while the bookmark is its
122	only holder.
123	
124	- conflicts with `main` are resolved in merge commits, never by rewriting published rungs
125	- a rebase is never required for correctness: it is a linearity preference
126	- coordinated rebases stay available (the bar is on unilateral rewrites, not rewrites), at the
127	  known cost of staling the git-SHA citations in the records; chids and ochid trailers survive
128	  a rebase
129	- once the bookmark's history is fully merged into `main` the bookmark is redundant and may be
130	  deleted
131	
132	The contrast with a cycle bookmark is the whole point: that one is a draft and may be rewritten
133	freely until it lands (see [Topic bookmarks are drafts](cycle.md#topic-bookmarks-are-drafts)),
134	this one is published and may not. Refined 2026-08-03 in vc-x1 from the earlier "treated as
135	permanent, never rebased" wording, after the fully merged `refactor-vc-x1` bookmark was deleted.
136	
137	## Resolvability
138	
139	A change ID travels with its commit: a **pushed** commit resolves to the same chid in every

200	## custom.md: the project layer
201	
202	[custom.md](custom.md) is an agent-file like the others, and the aim is that it stays as generic

## custom.md: the project layer

[custom.md](custom.md) is an agent-file like the others, and the aim is that it stays as generic
as they do. It holds only what a pinned file structurally cannot.

**Its skeleton is shared even though its content cannot be.** custom.md is never pinned, since
every project's content differs by construction. What converges is the section set: two `##`
headers, in this order, each meaning the same thing everywhere. A project's file is the payload's
skeleton with the angle brackets filled in, so a diff against the payload shows substitutions and
no structure.

- **`## Medium and validation`**: the medium and its validation commands (what the per-commit
  checklist's "validate the artifact" runs), what a version bump promises this artifact's users,
  and versioning specifics beyond [versioning.md](notes/versioning.md). Not a divergence and not
  negotiable, since another medium could not adopt them if it wanted to.
- **`## Project conventions and overrides`**: project-local conventions, and overrides of the
  pinned files; an override names the section it supersedes. **Empty at birth, and it should
  usually stay that way**: a rule the project would keep is still a *proposal* until it is
  rejected, so by default it belongs in the pinned file where the rule lives (see
  [Changing the agent-files](#changing-the-agent-files)), where it shows up as a diff. Writing it
  here instead hides it from exactly the review that should decide it. An empty section stays,
  with `_None._` under it, so the skeleton is one shape rather than a shape per project.

**A further layer is optional, and this file leaves it unnamed on purpose.** custom.md's intro
points at whatever the project carries beside it, read when present and absent when the project has
no wider context to answer to. The indirection is the point: the pinned set stays ignorant of what
that layer contains, so `AGENTS.md` -> `custom.md` -> whatever-else is one chain a project extends
without touching anything pinned, and a pinned file never has to name a concept some member does
not have.

content.text:
`custom.md` is now 15 lines with nothing to substitute — the payload default verbatim.

## What moved

**Out of `custom.md`:** the `<project>` in the title (now `# custom.md - the project layer`),
`## Medium and validation`, and everything else project-specific. What is left is the intro, the
pointer, and one empty section.

**Into `custom-family.md`:** `## Medium and validation` as its first section, ahead of Membership,
Messaging, and the Dogfood log. Its title became "iiac-perf's layer, as a member of the vc-x1
agent-file family", and its intro states the convention that makes this coherent:

> A member keeps `custom.md` byte-identical to the payload and puts everything of its own here.
> That buys a property worth having: `diff custom.md <template>/work/custom.md` is empty for every
> member, so the one file that can never be pinned still converges. The medium is here for that
> reason rather than because it has anything to do with the family.

## The ripple, which was the interesting part

Moving the medium out of `custom.md` broke every pinned file that pointed at `custom.md` *by name*
for the medium — `cycle.md` twice, `code.md`, `versioning.md`, plus the five satellite headers. I
did not repoint them at `custom-family.md`, because that would put a family filename in the pinned
set, which is what we just spent this whole pass removing.

Instead `AGENTS.md` Terminology gained a definition:

> **Project layer.** `custom.md` plus any further layer it points at, taken together. The pinned
> files name *the layer* and never a filename inside it, so a project can hold its medium and its
> conventions in `custom.md` or push them down into a layer below without a single pinned file
> changing.

Nine references now say "the [project layer]" instead of "custom.md". That is what lets both
arrangements be valid without the pinned set knowing which one a project chose.

## One question this opens, and my answer in the text

If the payload's `custom.md` has no `## Medium and validation`, where does a **non-member** put
theirs? I wrote it as: they add the section to their own `custom.md`, which is a normal
customization of their own file, and the payload simply does not pre-create it. `AGENTS.md` says so
explicitly rather than leaving it to be inferred.

The alternative is that the payload ships a placeholder Medium section that members then delete,
which puts every member back to differing from the payload. I went the other way, but tell me if
you would rather the payload carry the placeholder.

I have not yet updated the message to vc-x1 for this round of changes — it still describes the
previous split where `custom.md` kept the medium. Say the word and I will bring it in line.

message.content: A non-family member would put it in their custom.md or they can modify any agent-file as they see fit, with in winksaville repos they'll be a few family members the reminder I'll recommend/force them to use custom.md. As for the agent-files pointing at or mentioning custom.md I don't see why they need to change, the bot should logically follow the one line directive in our common family format. I maybe be missing something or so ask questions!

content.text: You're right, and my ripple was solving a problem the pointer already solves. Reverting it.

input.old_string:
[custom.md](custom.md) is the head of the [project layer](#terminology) and, unlike the pinned
files, it is never pinned: every project's content differs by construction. It ships from the
payload holding nothing but its own shape, so a project that changes nothing still has a valid one.

- **`## Project conventions and overrides`**: project-local conventions, and overrides of the
  pinned files; an override names the section it supersedes. **Empty at birth, and it should
  usually stay that way**: a rule the project would keep is still a *proposal* until it is
  rejected, so by default it belongs in the pinned file where the rule lives (see
  [Changing the agent-files](#changing-the-agent-files)), where it shows up as a diff. Writing it
  here instead hides it from exactly the review that should decide it. An empty section stays,
  with `_None._` under it, so the file is one shape rather than a shape per project.
- **The medium and its validation commands** (what the per-commit checklist's "validate the
  artifact" runs), and what a version bump promises this artifact's users, go somewhere in the
  project layer. A project with no further layer adds a `## Medium and validation` section here; a
  project with one may keep it there instead. The pinned files ask the layer, never the file.

**A further layer is optional, and this file leaves it unnamed on purpose.** custom.md's intro
points at whatever the project carries beside it, read when present and absent when the project has
no wider context to answer to. The indirection is the point: the pinned set stays ignorant of what
that layer contains, so `AGENTS.md` -> `custom.md` -> whatever-else is one chain a project extends
without touching anything pinned, and a pinned file never has to name a concept some project does
not have.

**A project whose further layer holds everything leaves custom.md byte-identical to the payload**,
which is worth doing where it is possible: it makes the one file that can never be pinned converge
anyway, checkable with a single `diff`, and it puts the project's whole customization surface in
one place.

Precedence: custom.md is loaded last and wins conflicts with this file and the satellites.

[custom.md](custom.md) is the project's own layer and, unlike the pinned files, is never pinned:
every project's content differs by construction. It ships from the payload holding nothing but its
own shape, so a project that changes nothing still has a valid one, and a project adds whatever it
needs: the medium and its validation commands, what a version bump promises this artifact's users,
and its conventions.

**`## Project conventions and overrides` is empty at birth and should usually stay that way.** A
rule the project would keep is still a *proposal* until it is rejected, so by default it belongs in
the pinned file where the rule lives (see [Changing the agent-files](#changing-the-agent-files)),
where it shows up as a diff. Writing it here instead hides it from exactly the review that should
decide it. An empty section stays, with `_None._` under it, rather than being deleted.

**custom.md may point at a further file**, which is then read as part of this layer. Where a
project keeps a given fact is that project's business, so nothing pinned names the further file or
knows what is in it: the chain is `AGENTS.md` -> `custom.md` -> whatever-else, and a pinned file
asking for something "in custom.md" is answered by following the pointer it finds there. That is
what lets a project with a wider context to answer to carry it without a single pinned file
changing, and a project with none carry nothing.

content.text:
Reverted. You were right — the pointer does the work, so nothing pinned had to change.

## What I undid

All nine repointed references are back to naming `custom.md` verbatim: the five satellite headers,
`cycle.md`'s two validation steps, `code.md`'s medium note, and `versioning.md`'s promise note. The
`Project layer` term I invented in Terminology is gone too. `agent-data/` and `notes/versioning.md`
now differ from the payload only where this configuration genuinely proposes something.

## What carries the weight instead

`custom.md`'s pointer, which is unpinned and therefore free to be as explicit as it needs:

> **If `custom-family.md` is present beside this file, read it too, as part of this layer.** Anything
> a pinned file expects to find "in custom.md" may live there instead, the medium and its validation
> commands included.

`AGENTS.md` still says the mechanism exists once, in its `custom.md` section, but names no file and
makes no claim about what is in it: "a pinned file asking for something 'in custom.md' is answered by
following the pointer it finds there." Hard rule 0 gained four words ("Follow any further file it
points at"); the File map and Terminology gained a clause each.

## Questions, since you invited them

**1. Does the payload's `custom.md` ship with a `## Medium and validation` placeholder?**

Right now it does not, and a non-member adds the section themselves. Your answer suggests you are
fine with that, since you said they can modify any agent-file as they see fit. The reason I did not
add one: if the payload carries a Medium section, every family member deletes it, so no member's
`custom.md` matches the payload any more, and the property you described ("family members have the
default `work/custom.md`") stops holding. Confirm and I will leave it out.

**2. Is `## Project conventions and overrides` the right and only section in the default?**

It is the one place a non-member's overrides go, and it is where the family's "should usually be
empty" discipline bites. But a non-member who puts their medium in `custom.md` would be adding a
section the payload never mentioned. That is fine by your rule, just worth saying out loud.

**3. The title.** I made it `# custom.md - the project layer` so there is no `<project>` to
substitute. That means a member's `custom.md` is byte-identical to the payload with zero edits,
which I think is what you were after. The cost is that the file no longer names which project it
belongs to. Worth it?

**4. Does the medium really belong in a file called `custom-family.md`?** It is there only because
of the family's keep-`custom.md`-pristine convention, not because cargo commands have anything to do
with the family. I wrote that reason into `custom-family.md`'s intro so it does not read as a
category error, but if it still grates, the alternative is that members do put their medium in
`custom.md` and accept one section of divergence from the payload.

I have not touched the vc-x1 message yet for this round — it still describes the earlier split where
`custom.md` kept the medium. I will bring it in line once these four settle.

[custom.md](custom.md) is the project's own layer and, unlike the pinned files, is never pinned:
every project's content differs by construction. It ships from the payload holding nothing but its
own shape, so a project that changes nothing still has a valid one, and a project adds whatever it
needs: the medium and its validation commands, what a version bump promises this artifact's users,
and its conventions.

**`## Project conventions and overrides` is empty at birth and should usually stay that way.** A
rule the project would keep is still a *proposal* until it is rejected, so by default it belongs in
the pinned file where the rule lives (see [Changing the agent-files](#changing-the-agent-files)),
where it shows up as a diff. Writing it here instead hides it from exactly the review that should
decide it. An empty section stays, with `_None._` under it, rather than being deleted.

**custom.md may point at a further file**, which is then read as part of this layer. Where a
project keeps a given fact is that project's business, so nothing pinned names the further file or
knows what is in it: the chain is `AGENTS.md` -> `custom.md` -> whatever-else, and a pinned file
asking for something "in custom.md" is answered by following the pointer it finds there. That is
what lets a project with a wider context to answer to carry it without a single pinned file
changing, and a project with none carry nothing.

### The family layer splits out of `custom.md`, and `work/custom.md` shrinks to a stub

wink diffed our `custom.md` against `work/custom.md` and the two files do not even begin the same.
Chasing that produced a sharper test than "do the sections match", and both files failed it:
**`work/custom.md` should be usable as-is by a project that has never heard of us.** It is not. It
carries a member name, a template path, and a conventions section whose real subject is what a
member owes the family. Ours was worse, with a dogfood log whose status vocabulary reads
`adopted family-wide`.

wink's design, which is tighter than what we first proposed: **`work/custom.md` becomes a stub with
nothing to substitute, and a member differs from it by exactly one line.** Everything a member
customizes moves into a `custom-family.md` beside it, reached by a single convention entry.

**Proposed `work/custom.md`**, entire:

```markdown
# custom.md - the project layer

The project's own layer over the pinned agent-files (see
[AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md#custommd-the-project-layer)). Loaded last; on conflict, this file wins.

## Project conventions and overrides

Project-local conventions, and overrides of the pinned files; an override names the section it
supersedes. A project whose further layer holds these keeps this section empty.

_None._
```

Note the title: no `<project>` to substitute, so a project that changes nothing still has a valid
file. **Ours is that file with the last line replaced by `- Read ./custom-family.md.`** and nothing
else, which you can check with one `diff`.

Then `custom-family.md` holds what we actually customize:

```markdown
# custom-family.md - <project>'s layer, as a member of the vc-x1 agent-file family

Read after [custom.md](custom.md), whose single convention entry points here. Present only in a
member repo; a project that is not a member does not carry this file.

## Medium and validation
   <the medium, the version-bump promise, full and fast validation commands>

## Membership
   <member name; template repository path>

## Messaging
   <the mailbox rules that decide how a session behaves; protocol governs>

## Dogfood log
   <_None._ at birth>
```

The medium is in there because of the keep-`custom.md`-pristine convention, not because cargo
commands have anything to do with the family; our copy says so in its intro so it does not read as
a category error.

**Nothing pinned needs to change for any of this, which is the part worth checking.** We tried the
other way first, repointing nine references in `cycle.md`, `code.md`, `versioning.md` and the
satellite headers from "custom.md" to a newly defined "project layer", and wink rejected it: the bot
reads `custom.md`, meets a one-line directive, and follows it, so a pinned file asking for something
"in custom.md" is already answered. All nine are reverted and byte-identical to your payload again.
`AGENTS.md` gained one clarifying sentence, that an entry which only points at a further file is not
an override and owes no "why not family-wide" justification, since otherwise our own one-liner would
