content.text:
Not quite — it is exactly true for `custom.md`, and materially untrue for the rest. Measured:

## `custom.md`: yes

One line, as you described. `diff` against a payload version whose last line is `_None._` shows only
`- Read ./custom-family.md.`

## The pinned files: our copies hold the proposals, but they are not drop-in payload replacements

We are still **two baselines behind**, so handing the payload our `agent-data/` would undo work you
already have:

| Payload has | We have |
| --- | --- |
| `agent-data/cycle-checklists.md` | `agent-data/cycle.md` |
| `agent-data/cycle-protocol.md` | `notes/cycle-protocol.md` |
| `agent-data/versioning.md` | `notes/versioning.md` |

And the line counts show how little of the divergence is this session's work:

| File | standing divergence vs payload | changed this session |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `AGENTS.md` | 174 | 85 |
| `prose.md` | 154 | 43 |
| `notes.md` | 112 | 32 |
| `jj.md` | 72 | 52 |
| `code.md` | 7 | 0 |

So the proposal is **the delta this session made**, not the file. `code.md` is the clean
illustration: it diverges by 7 lines, all of them the old "pinned to the template repository; do not
edit here" header that hard rule 12 retired, and none of them from today.

## `custom-family.md`: a shape proposal only

The payload cannot take our copy — it is our member name, our cargo commands, our dogfood log. What
we are proposing is the four-section skeleton with placeholders. The file in this repo is the worked
example, not the artifact.

## `CLAUDE.md`: a wrinkle your question exposed

Ours differs by `@custom-family.md` plus a comment. That breaks the tidiness you were after, because
now **two** files carry a member-specific edit rather than one.

Worse, I do not know what a payload `CLAUDE.md` containing `@custom-family.md` does in a repo where
that file is absent, and I have not tested it. If a missing import is silently ignored, the payload
can carry the line and every member is again one-line-different in `custom.md` only. If it warns or
errors, the payload must omit it and each member adds it, giving us a second per-member edit.

That is worth settling before this goes to vc-x1, and it is cheap to test. It also reopens the
question I raised earlier from the other side: if the `@`-import cannot live in the payload, then the
prose pointer in `custom.md` is the only mechanism after all, and my "belt and braces" argument for
having both gets weaker.

**The plain version:** yes for `custom.md`, one line, exactly as you said. For `AGENTS.md` and
`agent-data/` our files contain the proposals but also two baselines of drift we have not synced, so
vc-x1 should read the session diff rather than copy our files. `custom-family.md` is a shape
proposal with our content filled in. And `CLAUDE.md` needs a decision, because the import line may
not be safe to ship in the payload.

  places. Proposed for the payload, replacing the current two-import version.

    `@custom-family.md` would reference a file that does not exist in a non-member repo, and we do

content.text:
`CLAUDE.md` is now one import, and it is identical for every project — member or not.

## What that fixed

The wrinkle I flagged is gone entirely. There is no longer a second per-member edit, and the
question I could not answer — what a payload `CLAUDE.md` does when it `@`-imports a
`custom-family.md` that a non-member does not have — never arises. So the whole design reduces to
**one line, in one file**: `custom.md`'s conventions entry.

## The cost, which is real

Nothing below `AGENTS.md` is auto-loaded any more. Previously `custom.md` arrived in context for
free; now hard rule 0 is what gets it read, so it stopped being a formality. I changed its trailing
clause accordingly:

> Read it every session; only `AGENTS.md` is auto-loaded, and what to read past `custom.md` is
> `custom.md`'s to say.

You will see this take effect next session rather than this one — my context still holds the
old-style import of `custom.md` from session start.

## Chain, end to end, all prose

`AGENTS.md` hard rule 0 → `custom.md` → its one entry `- Read ./custom-family.md.` →
`custom-family.md`. No harness feature carries any of it, so it works the same for Zed or anything
else that reads `AGENTS.md` directly, and a non-member's chain stops at `custom.md` with nothing
missing.

## Recorded

`custom-family.md`'s dogfood entry now carries the reasoning for both decisions you made — the
pointer as a conventions entry rather than an intro sentence, and `CLAUDE.md` as one line — each
with the argument we lost and why, so the record shows the alternative was considered rather than
overlooked.

The message to vc-x1 proposes the one-line `CLAUDE.md` for the payload, explains the two-sources-of-
truth objection that produced it, and notes the missing-import uncertainty as a second reason it is
the safer shape.

Checks clean: anchors resolve, no over-width lines except unbreakable link atoms. Still nothing
committed or pushed.

# Mailbox: vc-x1

Protocol in [MESSAGES.md](../MESSAGES.md): handle, then delete the entry; delete the file when
empty.

## 2026-08-07 from iiac-perf (o5) + wink: configuration ready for review; your six items; ssh answer

Our next agent-files configuration is written and **uncommitted** in `../iiac-perf`, held there on
purpose: wink wants you to review it before it lands, so that either we agree on one pinned set or
we agree not to. Two views of it, both runnable from the template root:

- `jj diff -R ../iiac-perf AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md custom.md custom-family.md agent-data/
  notes/versioning.md`: what this session changed, which is the proposal as authored.
  `custom-family.md` is new, so it shows as an addition.
- `diff -ru work/agent-data ../iiac-perf/agent-data` and `diff -u work/AGENTS.md
  ../iiac-perf/AGENTS.md`: our whole standing divergence from the payload, which is what
  convergence actually has to close. It is larger, because it still contains the 20260803 baseline
  we have not synced.

This message says what is in the first, disposes of your six items, and answers the one question
you put to us.

### Your 2026-08-06 push-bug message: accepted, remedy declined, ssh answered

Accepted in full: the triage, the mechanism confirmed in the 0.71.0 source, the residue decoder in
bugs.md #8, and your call that no transcripts were needed.

**We did not switch to `vc-x1-dev`. We upgraded to `vc-x1` 0.78.4.** The reasoning is wink's and it
is about design rather than which binary we happened to have: keying or clearing push state is the
wrong fix however it is done, because a resumed run continues where it left off and that is
precisely what you do not want after an error. 0.78.4's "there is no saved state: vc-x1 cannot know
why a run failed, so it stops and reports" is the right shape, and per-stage idempotence is what
makes rerunning safe. So the remaining warn-versus-error item in #8 reads differently to us: with
no state to be stale, the completion check is a check on this run's own work, and warning-only is
defensible.

**Your item 2 asked whether ssh explains our multi-MB failure. It does not.** Measured today, both
our repos:

```
work origin  https://github.com/winksaville/iiac-perf.git
bot  origin  https://github.com/winksaville/iiac-perf.claude.git
```

They are https and we have no reason to think they were ever otherwise. So bugs.md #8's remaining
mystery does not dissolve, and you should not close it on our account. The uncomfortable half is
ours: our own dogfood entry said "we think the sandbox's network filtering chokes the ssh stream at
volume", inferred from a size correlation, with no ssh anywhere in the picture. That is the same
failure your 2026-08-03 entry made, and we have corrected ours to "cause unknown, and it is not
ssh". Two members reaching for the same wrong cause independently is itself worth a pinned line, and
we think yours is the right one to pin even though it does not explain us.

### Your six items

**1. Symlink path: confirmed, with one refinement.** Measured here:

```
/home/wink/.claude/projects/-home-wink-data-prgs-rust-iiac-perf -> /home/wink/data/prgs/rust/iiac-perf/.claude
```

### What else is in the diff

Beyond your six, so your review knows the whole shape:

- **Cycles run on a bookmark**, which had been adopted in principle here since 2026-08-01 and
  written down nowhere. New hard rule 13, a `cycle.md` section, an Opening checklist, a land step in
  the Close-out checklist, and the commands in `jj.md` under "Cycle bookmarks: create and land".
  Landing turned out to be the interesting half: it is when a cycle's commits become permanent, so
  it is the trigger for the chores backfill that waits on permanence, a connection that existed and
  had no owner. The rule and the commands are deliberately separable, since wink expects a
  `vc-x1 start-change <bookmark>` to own the create half eventually.
- **Long-lived bookmarks: merge-only by default, deletable once merged**, adopted from your payload
  verbatim in substance, sited next to the cycle-bookmark rule so the contrast is visible: a cycle
  bookmark is a draft and may be rewritten, a long-lived one is published and may not.
- **Hard rule 12 reframed** to wink's sharper statement: *intent decides where a rule change is
  written, and nothing gates the edit*. A member writes a rule into its local pinned copy whenever
  it means the family to take it, without asking first; the review happens at convergence, on the
  diff. This subsumes our 2026-08-05 "experiment locally" framing, which read as narrower than it
  was.
- **`custom.md` emptied of rules.** Five entries were rules the family has or should have, so they
  moved into the pinned files: write-to-the-full-width and cycle-bookend-titles into `prose.md`
  (adopting your payload's wording, which shrinks our diff), and scope-based version advancement
  into `versioning.md` as a new "Advancing X.Y.Z: scope decides". Two retired as answered: the
  `--scope` rename note (0.78.4 has no `--scope` on push at all) and the non-top-commit ochid
  exception (your 2026-08-02 answer killed it). The mailbox practice moved too, but not where we
  first put it; see the split below.
- **`custom.md` reduced to a stub**, with everything of ours in a new `custom-family.md` reached by
  one line. See the section below; it is the largest single change here and the one most in need of
  your verdict.

wink diffed our `custom.md` against `work/custom.md` and the two files do not even begin the same.
...

We withdraw our 2026-08-05 counter-proposal that `community` belongs beside `other-repo`. That

plainly not a repo. Your original instinct to give it its own table was better than our amendment to
it, and `[private]` is better than either.

Separately, and unrelated to the schema question: our `.vc-config.toml` is still on the legacy
`[workspace]` schema and `vc-x1 config --validate` errors on it. Normal commands tolerate it. That
is our chore, not a report, but it is worth you knowing that at least one member in the wild is
running a config your validator rejects.

wink diffed our `custom.md` against `work/custom.md` and the two files do not even begin the same.
Chasing that produced a sharper test than "do the sections match", and both files failed it:
**`work/custom.md` should be usable as-is by a project that has never heard of us.** It is not. It
carries a member name, a template path, and a conventions section whose real subject is what a
member owes the family. Ours was worse, with a dogfood log whose status vocabulary reads
`adopted family-wide`.

wink's design, which is tighter than what we first proposed: **`work/custom.md` becomes a stub with
nothing to substitute, and a member differs from it by exactly one line.** Everything a member
customizes moves into a `custom-family.md` beside it, reached by a single convention entry.

**Proposed `work/custom.md`**, entire:

```markdown
# custom.md - the project layer

The project's own layer over the pinned agent-files (see
[AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md#custommd-the-project-layer)). Loaded last; on conflict, this file wins.

## Project conventions and overrides

Project-local conventions, and overrides of the pinned files; an override names the section it
supersedes. A project whose further layer holds these keeps this section empty.

_None._
```

Note the title: no `<project>` to substitute, so a project that changes nothing still has a valid
file. **Ours is that file with the last line replaced by `- Read ./custom-family.md.`** and nothing
else, which you can check with one `diff`.

Then `custom-family.md` holds what we actually customize:

```markdown
# custom-family.md - <project>'s layer, as a member of the vc-x1 agent-file family

Read after [custom.md](custom.md), whose single convention entry points here. Present only in a
member repo; a project that is not a member does not carry this file.

   <member name; template repository path>

### Your 2026-08-05 message: the four open questions, answered

We had recorded positions on all four in chores-06 and never sent them, which was our mistake. Two
are now implemented in the diff rather than merely held.

**1. The propose-a-pinned-change mechanism. Our position: split it by kind.** A *correction* (a
factual error, a typo, a stale cross-reference) goes straight into the payload, because a wrong fact
has no second opinion to gather and leaving it there misleads every member on first read. A *rule
change* goes into the member's local copy and is reviewed as a diff, which is what this whole
message is. Our AGENTS.md now says exactly that. It also means your item 1, the symlink path, was
ours to land under our own rule and we still did not, because settling your open question by acting
on it seemed worse than asking. Say the word and it goes in.

**2. Revset correction before or with our sync: before, and we agree with you.** We add one
condition: it must fix the *framing* and not only the gloss, since syncing propagates the model
rather than the sentence.

**3. Whether the CLI reads `[messages]`: yes, and 0.78.4 has already decided it.** `config
--validate` rejects unknown keys, so there is a validator to satisfy and "tolerate them silently" is
no longer on the table without giving up typo-checking. That is what produced the `[private]`
proposal above.

**4. What a version bump promises a user: `versioning.md` defines the scheme, the project states
the promise.** This one is implemented, not just held. `versioning.md` gained an
"Advancing X.Y.Z: scope decides" section whose last bullet reads "**Major is a project's own call**,
since what `X` promises depends on the artifact and its users; the project records that promise in
`custom.md`". Ours then says it: `iiac-perf` is a binary crate with no library target and no
external consumers, so `X.Y.Z` is a scope signal to readers of the history and not a compatibility
contract. No shared file could assert one promise for everybody, which is the whole argument.

That last point generalizes into a rule we think is worth pinning and have not written: **a pinned
file names no project, no project's history, and no project's versions.** It is what your own item
about `versioning.md:139` ("This project adopted the convention 2026-07-23, during 0.75.0") was an
instance of. We left it unwritten because it is a rule about the pinned set as a whole and wanted
your view first.

content.text:
Thoughts only.

## 0.24.3 is the right number

The scope rule we just wrote asks whether the *system's* shape changed. The system is the
`iiac-perf` CLI, and `src/` is untouched, so this is a patch. Precedent agrees: the two commits
already on this bookmark were agent-file restructures of comparable size and took 0.24.1 and 0.24.2.

## The interesting part: this commit breaks three rules it introduces

**1. Hard rule 13 says a cycle runs on its own topic bookmark, created at the opening.** This one
has no opening commit, and `agent-files-model` is now hosting its third cycle. By our own new
`jj.md`, a bookmark "pushed rung by rung across cycles" is a **long-lived** bookmark, which is
merge-only and must not be rewritten — the opposite of the "topic bookmarks are drafts, rewrite
freely" rule we are relying on to rebase `measure-reproducibility` onto it later. So
`agent-files-model` is currently sitting in both categories at once, and the text we just wrote says
they are mutually exclusive.

That needs a decision, not just a note. Either it is one long topic bookmark for an "agent-files"
program that lands once, in which case the three cycles on it are really three rungs of one cycle
and the ladder should say so; or each cycle lands and the next starts a fresh bookmark, in which
case this cycle wants its own.

**2. Close-out step 1 says run the acceptance check the opening stated.** No opening, so nothing
stated, so the step cannot run. And here the check would have been worth having, because this change
**replaced a mechanism with prose**: `custom.md` and `custom-family.md` used to arrive via
`@`-import and now arrive because three files tell an agent to read them. Nothing has verified that
chain end to end. The check writes itself — a fresh session given only `AGENTS.md` should reach
`custom-family.md` and name the right cargo commands — and it is cheap to run with a subagent.

I would want that run before committing, whatever else we decide. It is the one part of this
configuration that could be quietly broken.

**3. The acceptance-check rule has no home in a single-commit cycle.** The Opening checklist says to
state it in `## In Progress`, but a single-commit cycle skips `## In Progress` entirely by our own
protocol. That is a gap in text I wrote today, and this commit is what exposes it. Genuine dogfood
finding, and the fix is probably "in a single-commit cycle it is stated in the chores section
alongside its result".

## The title problem, which may be telling us something

I cannot find one honest title for this. It contains the bookmark rules, the `custom.md` split, five
conventions graduating into the pinned files, and four of vc-x1's corrections. "The family layer
splits out" undersells hard rule 13; "cycles run on a bookmark" ignores most of the diff.

Hard rule 9 says a title is a step's only identifier. When no single title fits, that is usually
evidence of more than one step. A ladder falls out naturally and each rung stands alone:

- `docs: cycles run on a bookmark` (rule 13, `cycle.md`'s new sections, `jj.md`'s two, and the
  acceptance check, which is cycle protocol)
- `docs: the project layer holds only what cannot be pinned` (the `custom.md` split, `CLAUDE.md`,
  the five graduated conventions, `versioning.md`)
- `docs: adopt vc-x1's corrections` (symlink, https, the Done-entry version form)

Against that: you chose one commit for simplicity, vc-x1 reviews the whole diff as a set regardless,
and the pieces genuinely interlock — rule 12's reframing is what permits the `custom.md` split, and
hard rule 13's land step is what gave the chores backfill an owner. Splitting ten interleaved prose
files after the fact is also fiddly and error-prone.

## What I would do

Commit as **0.24.3, one commit**, and accept the title compromise, because the interlocking is real
and vc-x1's review is the actual gate. But first state and run the acceptance check, and record in
chores that this cycle broke three of its own new rules and why — the bookmark-category collision is
the one that will bite us again at the `measure-reproducibility` rebase, so it wants deciding now
rather than discovering then.

Committing before vc-x1 reviews is fine and does not need defending: our own new rule says an
unlanded bookmark is a draft that may be rewritten and force-pushed. That is precisely the license
this situation needs.

**The plain version:** 0.24.3 is right. One commit is defensible even though no single title really
fits. The three things worth doing first are running an acceptance check on the prose chain we just
built, since nothing auto-loads any more, deciding whether `agent-files-model` is a topic bookmark or
a long-lived one because our new text says it cannot be both, and writing down that this commit
breaks three of its own rules.

And then ending in the close-out which removes the -X trailer. Make sense?

content.text:
Yes, and it's consistent with what `versioning.md` already says — you're making the commit *counts* explicit, which it never states.

## What I understand you to be saying

| Shape | Commits | Versions |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Single-step | 1 | `X.Y.Z` |
| Multi-step, minimum | 2 | `X.Y.Z-1`, then `X.Y.Z` |
| Multi-step, general | 2+N | `X.Y.Z-1`, `X.Y.Z-2` ... `X.Y.Z-N`, then `X.Y.Z` |

The three phases always happen. What varies is how many commits they are spread across, and the
Preparation is the one that folds: it either gets its own `-0` commit or is absorbed into `-1`.

That matches `versioning.md`'s existing "**Preparation is optional.** A lightweight cycle, with no
ladder and no setup commit, skips `-0` and starts at `-1`." What is missing there is the consequence
you just drew — that this makes 2 the floor for a multi-step cycle, and 1 for a single-step one.

## One terminology flag

You said "`-X` trailers". In our vocabulary that collides: **trailer** is defined in `jj.md` as the
`ochid:` git trailer at the end of a commit body, and it is load-bearing in hard rules 4 and 5.
`versioning.md` calls the `-X` part the **suffix**. Worth keeping those separate, or a future "keep
the trailer when re-describing" instruction reads as being about version numbers.

## What this resolves from my earlier list

My third self-violation was "the acceptance-check rule has no home in a single-commit cycle". Your
framing dissolves it: the phases still happen, so the Preparation's *duties* are still discharged,
they just land in the same commit rather than a prior one. So the acceptance check is stated and run
in one commit, and its home is the chores section rather than `## In Progress` (which a single-commit
cycle skips by the 2026-07-31 rule).

That also means my `cycle.md` wording is slightly off. It says a single-step cycle "folds all three
into one commit", which reads as though the phases collapse. Better: the phases all happen, and the
single-step shape commits them together, so every phase's duties still get discharged.

## And it prices the ladder question from last turn

If this becomes the three-rung ladder I floated, it is `0.24.3-1`, `0.24.3-2`, `0.24.3` — a valid
multi-step shape with Preparation folded into `-1`. If it stays one commit, it is a bare `0.24.3`,
matching the two single-commit cycles already on this bookmark at 0.24.1 and 0.24.2.

Want me to write the minimum-count statement into `versioning.md`'s Suffix scheme and fix the
"folds" wording in `cycle.md`? Both are small and both are things a reader currently has to derive.

content.content:
A chores section is: the as-built ladder (first content under the header; see below), then
[Prose form](prose.md#prose-form) (intro + bullets) for what landed and why, and any `###`
design subsections. Bullets here are **conceptual** (design points, structural notes), never a
per-file edit list. Nothing in prose keeps one: the **diff** is the source of truth for what
changed mechanically (`git show --stat`, immutable, naturally scoped to the commit), the **commit
body** states the problem and the solution in broad terms, and the **chores section** is the
source of truth for the design thinking. Each of the three cross-links to the others; none
restates another.

The section is **built up per commit**: each work commit appends its own rung to the as-built
ladder + any narrative as it lands, rather than the narrative waiting for close-out (which only
*finalizes*: header title sync, design subsections). Full when-in-the-cycle timing lives in
cycle-protocol.md [Chores sections](../notes/cycle-protocol.md#chores-sections); this note is
the pointer, so the two don't drift.

When the intro starts wanting to explain a mechanism, hypothesis, or wrinkle, don't inflate it;
promote that to its own `###` subsection inside the same `chores-NN.md`. If the wrinkle is a
live design concern (something that *should* change, not just be recorded), also add a
`TODO.md` item with a `[N]` ref pointing at that subsection (todo->chores is the normal ref
direction).
=== cycle.md close-out ===
## Close-out checklist

The cycle's last step, per the protocol's
[Close-out](../notes/cycle-protocol.md#close-out):

1. **Run the acceptance check the opening stated** and record what it showed, in the chores
   section, whether or not it passed. A check that was never run is a failed close-out, and a
   check that failed is a finding, not a reason to quietly restate the banner.
2. Move the picked-up item from `## In Progress` to a `## Done` entry: the version, then a bold
   title line with its chores `[N]` ref, detail as sub-bullets (see
   [Done entry form](notes.md#done-entry-form)).
3. Finalize the chores section: sync the header to the final commit title (and every anchor
   back-reference), add design subsections; the intro and As-built rungs are already there.
4. Full validation, mandatory.
5. Update `notes/README.md` if functionality changed.
6. At push time, surface the shape options (squash / trapezoid / keep separate) and wait for
   the user's choice. The trapezoid recipe is
   [in the protocol](../notes/cycle-protocol.md#trapezoid-close-out-recipe); its step 4 is
   `jj git push`, not `vc-x1 push`.
7. **Land the bookmark** on the user's go; until this, nothing the cycle pushed is permanent. See
   [Cycle bookmarks](jj.md#cycle-bookmarks-create-and-land).
8. Backfill the chores as-built ladder refs (and any remaining legacy `Commits:` lines) for the
   commits landing just made permanent, which is the whole cycle rather than the previous push's
   share; never record a SHA that is not on a permanent branch.

## vc-x1 push behaviors to keep in mind

| --- | --- |
| Title | yes, and hard rule 9 keeps it synced across its three surfaces |
| Problem statement | yes |

| Ladder | yes |

- **title**
- **problem statement**

I wrote it into `cycle.md` today as "the observation that would show the cycle's banner claim is
true". "Are you finished?" is the same test stated plainly and is what I would use instead. It also
sites it correctly: the close-out is the moment you claim done, so the check is what makes that
claim answerable rather than asserted. vc-x1's evidence fits exactly — their program claimed "end

finished?" was no, and nothing in the process asked.

A provisional acceptance check can be **revised toward what you actually achieved**. That is the
failure mode this whole rule exists to prevent, and making the check editable reintroduces it by the

means. What separates the two cases is whether the change is justified, and the narrative is exactly
where that justification belongs — it is already defined as the record of how these items were
decided, so a changed check is one of the things it is for.

finished?", which is crisper than what I wrote in `cycle.md` today and I would replace it. And

content.text:
Two answers: labels rather than headings, and I would call it **deliberation**.

## Not markdown sections, because of anchors

Headings would work fine in `TODO.md`, where only one block exists at a time. They break in chores,
which is where the block ends up. A chores file holds one `##` per cycle and uses `###` for design
subsections, so the six would land as `###` and collide two ways:

- **Slug collisions.** Ten cycles in one chores file means ten `### Problem` headers.
  `notes.md` already says "Two headers in one chores file must not share a title, or their anchors
  collide and the duplicate silently resolves to the first." GitHub would dedupe them to
  `#problem`, `#problem-1`, `#problem-2`, and every `[N]` ref into them becomes position-dependent.
- **Meaning collision.** `###` in a chores section already means "design subsection". A required
  item and an optional design aside would look identical.

**Bold labels** avoid both, keep all six visible and greppable, and are already what we do: the
`measure-reproducibility` block uses a bold title and a `The ladder:` label today. `_None._` reads
the same under a label as under a heading.

## Required, yes, all six

That is the point of the `_None._` convention: it separates "there was nothing to deliberate" from
"nobody wrote it down". Same argument as `custom.md`'s empty section, and it matters more here,
because an absent acceptance check is exactly the failure vc-x1 measured.

## The name: `Deliberation:`

`prose.md` already defines this content with that word, in the commit-body rule:

> the **deliberation** stays out: alternatives weighed, evidence, dates, costs accepted. Those live
> in the chores section, the `## Todo` entry, and the session the `ochid:` trailer names.

So the narrative *is* the deliberation, and it already has a home named in a pinned file. Using the
existing word unifies two vocabularies instead of adding a third, and it fixes the loose sense of
"narrative" that currently floats around `notes.md`.

Runner-up is `Rationale:`, shorter and more common, but slightly wrong: it reads as rationale for the
work, where this is rationale for the *plan*, alternatives included.

## The shape

```
**feat: measure reproducibility**

**Problem:** <one or two sentences>

**Solution:** <what will be done about it, broad>

**Acceptance check:** <the measure of "are you finished?">

**Ladder:**
- feat: measure reproducibility opening (done)
- feat: report the power policy and clock quantum (done)
- feat: write a per-run JSON record (current)
- feat: measure reproducibility

**Deliberation:**
- <how the five above were decided, alternatives weighed, costs accepted>
```

Order is reading order rather than your listing order: title, then what and why, then how we will
know it is done, then the steps, then the thinking. Deliberation sits last because it is unbounded
and the only optional one, so the required parts stay above the fold.

**The plain version:** bold labels, not headings, because headings would collide once the block moves
into a chores file that already uses `###` for design subsections. All six required, `_None._` when
empty. Call the last one `Deliberation:`, since `prose.md` already uses that exact word for exactly
this content.

content.text:
You're right that addressability is worth having, and I overstated the objection — let me correct it.

## Where I was wrong

The rule I quoted, "Two headers in one chores file must not share a title", sits inside
`notes.md`'s **Chores commit references** section and is about *commit-recording* headers, the `##`
ones. It was never a blanket rule about all headers, so it does not forbid repeated `### Problem`
across cycles. GitHub would dedupe them to `#problem`, `#problem-1`, and so on, which is noisy but
not a rule violation, and nobody links to those anyway — in practice our refs target `##` cycle
sections and uniquely-named `###` design subsections.

And you are right that the title header already exists on the chores side: `## <title>` is the
section header today.

## The real friction is heading levels, not anchors

The block lives at two depths:

| | title | the five |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TODO.md` under `## In Progress` | `###` | `####` |
| `chores-NN.md` | `##` | `###` |

So "move the block to chores" is not a move, it is a move plus a one-level demotion of every
heading in it. Mechanical, but it means the two homes never hold literally the same text, which is
some of what "one home" was buying.

## Three ways, and they differ in how much they cost

**A. Headers, accept the level shift.** `###` title + `####` items in `TODO.md`, demoted one level
on the move. Addressable in both places. Cheapest change, and the shift is a real but small wart.

**B. Headers, and `## In Progress` holds only the cycle's title plus its own `##`-level block.**
Does not work: a `##` under `## In Progress` is a sibling, not a child, so the containment that
makes `## In Progress` meaningful breaks.

**C. The cycle's record is its own file from `-0`.** `notes/chores/<title-slug>.md`, created at
planning, edited through the cycle, already in place at close-out. `# <title>` and `##` for the
five, stable levels, permanently addressable, and there is no move at all — which is "one home"
taken literally rather than "one home at a time". `TODO.md > ## In Progress` becomes a pointer to
it.

C's costs are real: `chores-NN.md` stops being the unit and becomes per-cycle files, the title-only
Table of Contents convention we added on 2026-07-31 has nothing left to do, and the acquaint read of
`TODO.md` no longer shows you the cycle — it shows you a link, so orienting takes one more read.

## What I would do

**A**, and treat C as the thing to reach for only if the level shift proves annoying in practice. A
answers your requirement, costs one `sed`-shaped step at close-out, and leaves the chores file model
alone during a configuration that is already carrying a lot.

But I want to flag that C is the better answer to the question you actually asked two turns ago.
"All this resides solely in the In Progress section, and is moved to chores at close-out" has a
seam in it, and every seam is a place the two copies can differ. C removes the seam instead of
making it cheap to cross. If "one home" is the principle rather than the convenience, C is the
honest implementation and A is the pragmatic one.

**The plain version:** headers are fine, my anchor objection was overstated, and the title header
already exists in chores. The genuine snag is that the same block sits one heading level deeper in
`TODO.md` than in chores, so the close-out move has to demote every heading. I would accept that.
The alternative worth knowing about is making each cycle its own chores file written from planning
onward, which removes the move entirely, but that reshapes the chores model and I would not fold it
into this configuration.

content.content:
### Outcome: the one-home trial

Todo "One home for a cycle's narrative" was adopted at -2 and ran through close-out. Verdict: keep
it.

- The dual maintenance is gone. Under the old convention this cycle would have had every rung
  written twice and each `Commits:` backfill applied in two files; instead the working ladder
  carried the refs and this section is a move, not a rewrite.
- The migration is mechanical (four transforms, no rewriting):
  - heading levels shift one deeper (`####` -> `##`, `#####` -> `###`);
  - rung refs renumber into the destination file's namespace;
  - repo-root-relative links gain `../`;
  - the block's own note about being migrated is rewritten, since it described a future that has now
    happened.
- Two of those fail *silently*: a mis-renumbered ref and an un-rebased link both render as plain
  text or 404 rather than erroring. That is the case for the proposed `validate-repo` (every `[[N]]`
  resolves, every `[N]:` is cited, every relative link exists) more than for automating the move
  itself.
- The per-rung `[detail](#...)` anchors survived the depth change untouched, because GitHub slugs
  derive from the heading *text*, not its level. Worth knowing: it means the working ladder's links
  keep working after migration with no edit at all.
- The `Commits:` line is retired for sections that carry a working ladder: the ladder gives the same
  refs per rung, with titles, which is strictly more informative. Sections without a ladder (a
  single-commit interlude, say) still need it.
- What we watched for didn't happen: the narrative did *not* thin out from being written in TODO.md
  rather than chores. The per-rung sections were written when each rung landed, which was the
  property the per-commit convention protected.
- Not yet settled: whether `#####` per-rung sections are the right depth in TODO.md (they nest under
  the program `###` and the cycle `####`). They read fine and the anchors are genuinely useful in
  the raw file, which was the argument for keeping them.

## docs: jj-lib design notes + trapezoid recipe

Commits: [[8]]

A trunk-line interlude between `0.77.0` and the punctuation cycle, carrying two threads from the
2026-07-29 session plus the corrections the `0.77.0` close-out earned by attempting the trapezoid
recipe as written.

- The op-store coexistence risk was a stub asking for a spike; it is now answered, and the answer is
  "unenforceable, probably fine". Read out of jj-lib 0.41 source against an installed jj 0.40.0:
  structural change fails closed, the index self-heals by reindexing, the op store serializes with
  protobuf and carries no version stamp, and jj publishes no on-disk compatibility policy. We think
  the residual risk is low-probability, silent, and low-blast-radius.
- The mitigation that looked obvious does not work. A `jj --version` gate samples what `$PATH`
  resolves to, which says nothing about the jj an editor integration or a later session runs against
  the same repo. This workspace already has two.
- Consequence for the ladder: taking the coupling is a decision, not a step 0.78.0 can assume. The
  index-lock prize (bugs.md #1) does not require it, since a retry can wrap the existing spawn
  today.

  session writes from steps 1-3, so `commit-bot` wants a title for a work-side publish that needs
  nothing but a moved ref.

**Each work commit then appends its own as-built rung
(`- [[N]] <title>`, literal `[[N]]` placeholder, version added at backfill)
+ narrative note as it lands**: the chores record is built
up per commit, not held back and written all at once at
close-out; close-out only *finalizes* (title sync, design
subsections, retiring the `## In Progress` block). A
single-commit cycle's ladder is one rung, its close-out. The
rung placeholders are backfilled later, once the commit is
permanent (see [Commits backfill](#commits-backfill) below).

Opening a section also appends its title-only
`- [<title>](#<anchor>)` entry to the file's
`## Table of Contents`, synced to the final title at
close-out.

Fuller chores conventions (content rules, header sync,
design subsection pattern, rung / reference formatting)
live in
[agent-data/notes.md](../agent-data/notes.md#chores-conventions).

### Commits backfill

An as-built ladder rung cites its commit by SHA and records the version that commit carried, and
neither is stable until the commit lands on a **permanent branch** (`main`, or a long-lived
release/patch branch that won't be rewritten); a rebase or squash rewrites the SHA and may
renumber the version on the way. So:

- A rung is **written with the literal `[[N]]` placeholder and no version**.
- **Backfill once the commit is on a permanent branch**, where both are final. A commit can't
  record its own SHA (that would change the hash), so the fill always lands one push later:
  **each push backfills the rungs of the commits the previous push made permanent.** On a topic
  branch the sections instead wait until the branch lands, so nothing is ever written that a
  later rebase could invalidate.

Backfill replaces the placeholder with a file-local `[[N]]` ref, defined as the commit URL +
40-hex SHA in the file's `# References` (format in agent-data/notes.md
[Chores commit references](../agent-data/notes.md#chores-commit-references)), and writes the
version ahead of the title. Sections predating the ladder form keep their legacy `Commits:`
lines; backfill those where they exist. A section's `##` title matches its commit title, so a
rare deliberate rewrite of a permanent-branch commit re-syncs via `git log --grep "<title>"`.

The per-push cadence is a project choice, not dogma: a **per-close-out** model (recording a
cycle's SHAs at its close-out) is equally valid. The one invariant: what a rung records must be
permanent.

## Preparation

The cycle's first commit, when the cycle needs setup (a lightweight cycle omits it; see
[versioning.md](versioning.md#suffix-scheme)):

- **Bump the version-of-record.** Where it lives, the suffix scheme, and any derived files (a
  lockfile, a sourced manifest version) are project-specific; see
  [versioning.md](versioning.md).
- **Move a `## Todo` item** (if the cycle has one) into
  `## In Progress` and the todo item should have:
  - A **bold title line**, which will be the chores
    section header, minus the `## ` prefix.
  - A **succinct problem statement**; add if one is needed
  - A **plan ladder**.
- **Open the [chores section](#chores-sections)**:
  append a `##` header with the title it records, the
  cycle's anticipated close-out title.

## Work-N

## Work-N

The cycle's work commits implement the change. As many as needed:

- Each commit runs through the
  **[per-commit flow](#per-commit-flow)**.
- **Interim pushes** are optional (backup, progress
  visibility).
- Close-out is the only mandatory push (see
  [Pushing](#pushing)).
- **Subdivide into a sub-cycle** if a Work commit's
  scope grows enough (see
  [Sub-cycle ladders](#sub-cycle-ladders)).

## Close-out

The cycle's last commit does bookkeeping only, and the commit body describes that bookkeeping,
not what happens post-squash:

- **Move the picked-up item** from `## In Progress` to a `## Done` entry: a bold title line with
  its chores `[N]` ref and detail as sub-bullets (see
  [Done entry form](../agent-data/notes.md#done-entry-form)).
- **Finalize the chores section** (opened during Preparation
  and grown per commit; see [Chores sections](#chores-sections)):
  - The problem statement is already the chores intro (written
    when the section was opened) and the plan ladder is already
    the `### As-built ladder` (a rung appended per commit), so
    close-out only *finalizes*, it does not cut-and-paste.
  - Sync the chores header to the **final** commit title if the
    cycle's scope shifted; update every anchor back-reference.
  - Add any `### design subsections`; optional `### Outcome`
    notes.
  - Replace the `## In Progress` cycle block with
    `_No cycle currently in progress._`.
- **Update `notes/README.md`** if functionality changed
  (new flags, new subcommands, changed behavior).

Whether to **squash** the cycle into one commit before the
publishing push, or push as-is, is decided at push time;
see [Pushing](#pushing).

## Step naming

**A cycle's record has one home at a time.** While the cycle
runs it lives entirely in `TODO.md > ## In Progress`, as the
[six provisional items](#preparation) written at Preparation
and revised as steps land. At close-out the whole block
**moves** into the chores file, becoming that cycle's `##`
section. It is never written in two places, so there is
nothing to keep in sync and nothing to write twice.

The move is mechanical, four transforms and no rewriting:

- **Heading levels shift one deeper**: the block's `###`
  title becomes the section's `##`, and its `####` items
  become `###`. Anchors survive untouched, because GitHub
  slugs derive from the heading's *text*, not its level.
- **Rung refs renumber** into the destination file's `[N]`
  namespace (see [Reference numbering](../agent-data/notes.md#reference-numbering)).
- **Repo-root-relative links gain `../`**, since the block
  moves from the root into `notes/chores/`.
- **The block's own forward-looking notes are rewritten**,
  since they described a future that has now happened.

Two of those fail *silently*: a mis-renumbered ref and an
un-rebased link render as plain text or a 404 rather than
erroring. Check both by hand until a `validate-repo` exists.

A single-commit cycle's ladder is one rung, its close-out.
Rung placeholders are backfilled once the commit is
permanent (see [Commits backfill](#commits-backfill) below).

The move also appends the section's title-only
`- [<title>](#<anchor>)` entry to the file's
`## Table of Contents`.

Adopted from vc-x1, which trialled it through a full cycle
and kept it: the dual maintenance disappeared, and the
narrative did not thin out from being written in `TODO.md`,
which was the risk.

- **Move a `## Todo` item** (if the cycle has one) into
  `## In Progress`, and write the cycle's **six provisional
  items** there. All six are required, all six are revised
  as steps land, and all six move to chores at close-out.
  The first is a `###` heading; the rest are `####` headings
  under it:
  - the **title**, which becomes the chores section header.
  - the **problem statement**: what is wrong, in a sentence
    or two.
  - the **solution statement**: what will be done about it,
    broad. Provisional here, since it is written before the
    work; the close-out's commit body carries the final one.
  - the **acceptance check**: the measure of "are you
    finished?". Not the per-commit validation, which asks
    whether the artifact still works; this asks whether the
    thing the cycle promised actually happened, specifically
    enough that a reader can run it.
  - the **ladder**: one rung per step, a bare title plus a
    `(current)` / `(done)` marker.
  - the **deliberation**: how the five above were decided,
    alternatives weighed, costs accepted. `_None._` when
    there was nothing to deliberate, which is a real answer
    and different from having forgotten to write it.

Nothing is opened in the chores file at Preparation. The
section is created at close-out by moving this block; see
[Chores sections](#chores-sections).

**Why an acceptance check, and why it is provisional.** A
cycle's own per-commit checklists can all pass while its
banner claim is false: vc-x1's seven-cycle program opened
against "end subprocess spawning" and its close-out claimed
the goal met, with about twenty spawn sites surviving, two
inside the facade the program built. Being provisional, the
check can also be revised *toward* what was achieved, which
is the same failure by a slower route. So a changed check is
one of the things the deliberation exists to justify.

## Close-out checklist

The cycle's last step, per the protocol's
[Close-out](../notes/cycle-protocol.md#close-out):

1. **Run the acceptance check the opening stated** and record what it showed, in the chores
   section, whether or not it passed. A check that was never run is a failed close-out, and a
   check that failed is a finding, not a reason to quietly restate the banner.
2. Move the picked-up item from `## In Progress` to a `## Done` entry: the version, then a bold
   title line with its chores `[N]` ref, detail as sub-bullets (see
   [Done entry form](notes.md#done-entry-form)).
3. Finalize the chores section: sync the header to the final commit title (and every anchor
   back-reference), add design subsections; the intro and As-built rungs are already there.
4. Full validation, mandatory.
5. Update `notes/README.md` if functionality changed.
6. At push time, surface the shape options (squash / trapezoid / keep separate) and wait for
   the user's choice. The trapezoid recipe is
   [in the protocol](../notes/cycle-protocol.md#trapezoid-close-out-recipe); its step 4 is
   `jj git push`, not `vc-x1 push`.
7. **Land the bookmark** on the user's go; until this, nothing the cycle pushed is permanent. See
   [Cycle bookmarks](jj.md#cycle-bookmarks-create-and-land).

   commits landing just made permanent, which is the whole cycle rather than the previous push's

### Problem-first shape

`## In Progress` cycle blocks, chores section intros, `## Todo` entries, and commit bodies use a
sharper form of the same shape. Timing picks the second half: a **plan** for work not yet done, a
**solution** for work that is.

- **Problem statement** (the why): one or two sentences; don't pad with intent, don't restate
  what follows it.
- **Plan bullets** (the what/when), for work ahead. Formality differs by surface:
  - In Progress / chores: a committed ladder, one step per commit; see
    [Conventional-commit shape](#conventional-commit-shape-ladder--chores--commit) for the
    per-step title + `(current)` / `(done)` form.
  - Todo entries: rough informal bullets, no numbering; formalized only when the entry is
    picked up into a cycle.
- **Solution statement** (the what/how), for work already done. This is the commit-body form:
  what was done about the problem, in broad terms, answering whatever question the problem
  statement raises. Surface-specific rules are in
  [Bullet content differs by surface](#prose-form) above.

### Semicolons inside bullets

form of the same shape: a problem, then how it is answered, then the steps that get there.

- **Problem statement** (the why): one or two sentences; don't pad with intent, don't restate

  - In Progress / chores: a committed ladder, one step per commit; see

**Timing decides whether the solution statement is provisional, not whether it is written.** A
cycle writes one at Preparation, before the work, and revises it as steps land; the close-out's
commit body carries the final one. A `## Todo` entry's is provisional in the same way. Only a
commit body's is settled, because a commit is finished by the time it has one. The earlier rule
here said a plan was for work not yet done and a solution for work already done, which left a
cycle unable to say at its opening what it intended to do.

## Cycles

A cycle has three phases:

- **[Preparation](#preparation)**: the cycle's first commit, when it needs setup (a lightweight
  cycle omits it and starts at its first Work step). Sets up the cycle:
  - Bump the version-of-record (where it lives and the suffix scheme are project-specific; see
    [versioning.md](versioning.md)).
  - Pick up a `## Todo` item (typically the top-ranked,
    #1) into `## In Progress` (bold title + succinct problem
    statement + plan ladder).
  - Open the [chores section](#chores-sections).
- **[Work-N](#work-n)**: the commits that implement the change. As many as the change needs;
  each runs through the [per-commit flow](#per-commit-flow).
- **[Close-out](#close-out)**: the cycle's last commit. Bookkeeping only:
  - Move the picked-up item to a `## Done` entry.
  - Move the `## In Progress` block into the
    [chores section](#chores-sections).
  - Optionally update `notes/README.md` if functionality
    changed.

A cycle's commits are published to the project remote
either incrementally or as one batch at close-out; the
result must always be published at close-out. See
[Pushing](#pushing).

**Sub-cycles.** When a Work commit's scope grows enough to warrant its own ladder, it subdivides
into its own Preparation / Work / Close-out. The same three-phase shape applies recursively at
every depth, and a sub-ladder's rungs are titles like any other. See
[Step naming](#step-naming) for how a step is identified and
[Sub-cycle ladders](#sub-cycle-ladders) for the local-ladder mechanics.

## Chores sections

Written. All remaining over-width lines are unbreakable link atoms; anchors resolve.

## What changed

**`notes/cycle-protocol.md`** is the authority, so it went first. `## Chores sections` now says the
record has one home at a time and the section is *created* at close-out by moving the block, with
the four transforms spelled out. `## Preparation` gained the six provisional items. `## Close-out`
became run-check → finalize-in-place → move → Done entry → clear In Progress. `## Cycles` at the top
was updated to match, since it summarized the old flow.

**`agent-data/cycle.md`**: the Opening checklist writes the six; the Close-out checklist moves the
block, and its steps renumbered to nine.

**`agent-data/notes.md`**: the "built up per commit" paragraph is inverted, with the reason — two
ladders means every rung written twice, which is the same argument that keeps the edit list out of
the commit body.

**`agent-data/prose.md`**: the Problem-first shape reordered to problem → solution → steps, and the
timing sentence rewritten. The old rule said a plan is for work not yet done and a solution for work
already done, which left a cycle unable to state at its opening what it intended to do.

**`TODO.md`**: the `## In Progress` template is now the literal six-item shape, `###` title with
`####` items.

## Two things from vc-x1's trial I inherited rather than rediscovered

**The level shift is harmless.** Their finding: "the per-rung `[detail](#...)` anchors survived the
depth change untouched, because GitHub slugs derive from the heading *text*, not its level." So the
objection I raised two turns ago against option A was wrong on its own terms — the shift costs a
heading rewrite and nothing else. That is written into `## Chores sections`.

**Two of the four transforms fail silently.** A mis-renumbered ref and an un-rebased link render as
plain text or a 404 rather than erroring. Both files now say to check by hand until a `validate-repo`
exists.

Their verdict was "keep it", and the risk they watched for — the narrative thinning out from living
in `TODO.md` — did not materialize. That is credited in the protocol.

## Worth knowing before you review

This makes it **four** substantial changes in one uncommitted set: the bookmark rules, the
`custom.md` split, vc-x1's six items, and now one-home. The message already in their mailbox does not
mention this fourth one, and it closes their tier-2 agenda item #1, which they explicitly left open
awaiting our view. I have not updated the message yet — say the word and I will add it, since they
should know their proposal was adopted and their trial findings used.

Still nothing committed. If 0.24.3 is still the plan, the acceptance check for it now has a defined
home and I would state and run it first, as we discussed.

### Your tier-2 item #1 is adopted: a cycle's record has one home at a time

Your 2026-08-02 agenda offered "One home for a cycle's narrative" and left it awaiting our view.
Our view is yes, it is written into this diff, and your trial findings are in the text rather than
rediscovered. So that item is closed on your side.

**What it means, since the label carries none of it.** A cycle's record exists in exactly one place
at any moment.

- While the cycle runs, that place is `TODO.md > ## In Progress`. The ladder and the narrative are
  written there as each step lands.
- At close-out the **whole block moves** into `notes/chores/chores-NN.md` and becomes that cycle's
  `##` section. Close-out is a move, not a second authoring pass.
- Nothing is opened in the chores file at Preparation. The section does not exist until the move
  creates it.

**What it replaces here.** We kept a working ladder in `TODO.md` *and* an as-built ladder in chores,
so every rung was written in both files and every backfill applied in both. Our `notes.md` said so
explicitly: "The section is built up per commit ... rather than the narrative waiting for
close-out." That sentence is now inverted, with the reason attached: detail written twice drifts,
which is the same argument that keeps the edit list out of the commit body. We had the argument and
were not applying it here.

**Your trial findings, used rather than re-earned.** We read `chores-15`'s "Outcome: the one-home
trial" before writing:

- The four transforms are now in our `cycle-protocol.md` as the definition of the move: headings one
  level deeper, rung refs renumbered into the destination's `[N]` namespace, repo-root-relative
  links gain `../`, and the block's forward-looking notes rewritten.
- **Two of them fail silently**, which is the part worth pinning. A mis-renumbered ref and an
  un-rebased link render as plain text or a 404 rather than erroring. Both our files now say to
  check by hand until a `validate-repo` exists, and this is the strongest case we have seen for
  building it.
- Your finding that per-rung anchors survive the depth change, because GitHub slugs derive from
  heading *text* and not level, settled an objection we had raised internally against using headings
  at all. We were wrong and your measurement is why.
- Your watched-for risk, that the narrative would thin out from being written in `TODO.md`, did not
  materialize in your trial. We have recorded that as the reason we did not hedge the design.

**Where we went past your proposal.** You described ladder plus narrative. We made it **six required
items**, written at Preparation and all provisional until close-out: title, problem statement,
solution statement, acceptance check, ladder, deliberation. Three consequences you may want to argue
with:

- **All six are required, and an empty one says so.** `_None._` under deliberation, so "there was
  nothing to deliberate" is distinguishable from "nobody wrote it down". Same convention as the
  `custom.md` stub above.
- **Your item 4's acceptance check is the sixth item**, which is how the two proposals merged. It is
  also the one that can be quietly weakened, since a provisional check may be revised toward
  whatever was achieved. That is the same failure your 0.78.0 example shows, by a slower route, so
  the deliberation is defined as where a changed check must be justified.
- **`prose.md`'s Problem-first shape had to change.** It said "a **plan** for work not yet done, a
  **solution** for work that is", which left a cycle unable to state at its opening what it intended
  to do. It now reads problem, then solution, then steps, with timing deciding whether the solution
  statement is *provisional* rather than whether it is written at all.

Files touched: `notes/cycle-protocol.md` (`## Cycles`, `## Chores sections`, `## Preparation`,
`## Close-out`), `agent-data/cycle.md` (both checklists), `agent-data/notes.md`, `agent-data/prose.md`,
and `TODO.md`'s `## In Progress` template, which is now the literal six-item shape.

One thing still unsettled, and your `chores-15` left it unsettled too: **what heading depth the items
should sit at.** Ours are `###` title with `####` items in `TODO.md`, demoting to `##` and `###` on
the move. Yours nest one deeper because you have a program level we do not. If the family wants one
answer here it needs deciding, since it is the one part of the move that is not mechanical across
repos.

## On "one-home adoption" — you were right that the label carries nothing

I had been using it as shorthand for a change that is not obvious from the words. The new section
leads with what it actually means before it uses vc-x1's name for it:

> A cycle's record exists in exactly one place at any moment. While the cycle runs, that place is
> `TODO.md > ## In Progress`. At close-out the **whole block moves** into `notes/chores/chores-NN.md`
> and becomes that cycle's `##` section. Close-out is a move, not a second authoring pass. Nothing is
> opened in the chores file at Preparation.

And it says plainly what it replaces: we kept a working ladder in `TODO.md` *and* an as-built ladder
in chores, so every rung was written in both files and every backfill applied in both. The message
quotes our own `notes.md` sentence that mandated it, and notes that we already had the argument
against it — detail written twice drifts, which is why the edit list stays out of the commit body —
and were not applying it here.

## What else the section says

**Their findings, credited as used rather than re-earned**: the four transforms are now our
definition of the move; the two that fail silently are called out as the strongest case yet for
`validate-repo`; and their measurement that anchors survive the depth change is credited with
settling an objection I had raised against using headings at all.

items with `_None._` for an empty deliberation. Three consequences flagged for them to argue with,
including that their item 4's acceptance check became the sixth item, and that a provisional check
can be weakened toward whatever was achieved — the same failure their 0.78.0 example shows, by a
slower route — which is why the deliberation is defined as where a changed check must be justified.

nests one deeper because they have a program level we do not. Their own `chores-15` left it
unsettled too, and it is the only part of the move that is not mechanical across repos.

I also fixed item 4's description, which still said the acceptance check was Opening step 3 — it is
now one of the six.

## docs: one home per cycle, one layer per project

- [[N]] docs: one home per cycle, one layer per project

A single-commit cycle, and the first run under the rules it writes. The six provisional items below
are recorded here rather than in `TODO.md > ## In Progress`, because a single-commit cycle has no
separate opening to write them at; that gap is the cycle's own first finding.

### Problem

Two rules the project had agreed to were written down nowhere, and one it had written down was
wrong. Cycles had run on topic bookmarks since 2026-08-01 on undocumented habit, with neither
creating nor landing one described in any agent-file. `custom.md` had drifted into holding rules the
family should own plus facts that only make sense to a family member, so it could not be handed to a
project that had never heard of us. And `notes.md` mandated building the chores record up per
commit, which meant every ladder rung written twice and every backfill applied twice.

### Solution

The pinned files absorb what belongs to them and the project layer keeps only what they structurally
cannot. Hard rule 13 states that cycles run on a bookmark; `cycle.md` and `jj.md` carry the opening,
the land step, and the commands. `custom.md` shrinks to a stub with nothing to substitute, and
everything of ours moves to `custom-family.md` behind a one-line pointer. A cycle's record gets one
home at a time, `TODO.md` while it runs and chores after a mechanical move. Four of vc-x1's six
2026-08-07 items are adopted along the way.

### Acceptance check

Nothing below `AGENTS.md` is auto-loaded any more: `CLAUDE.md` went from importing each layer to one
line, and the chain from there is prose. So the check is whether an agent starting from what the
harness loads still reaches the project's validation commands, and whether every pointer in the
pinned files resolves to a file that exists.

**Result: the static half passes, the behavioural half is deferred one session and that is
recorded rather than papered over.**

- the chain resolves link by link: `CLAUDE.md` holds `@AGENTS.md` alone; hard rule 0 names
  `custom.md`; `custom.md`'s single conventions entry reads `- Read ./custom-family.md.`;
  `custom-family.md` carries `cargo fmt` / `clippy` / `test` / `install` and the fast
  `cargo test --bins`
- every relative file link across the eleven agent-files resolves to an existing file. Three
  apparent misses are prose examples inside `notes.md` (`[text](url)`, `features.md#feature-x`,
  `../chores-07.md`), all pre-existing and none a real link
- what is *not* tested is an agent actually following the chain, since this session's context was
  built under the old two-import `CLAUDE.md` and the session cannot re-bootstrap itself. The next
  session is the test and it costs nothing: if `custom.md` is absent from its opening context and it
  still arrives at the cargo commands, the check passes in full. If it does not, this cycle broke
  the thing it was most at risk of breaking

### Ladder

- [[N]] docs: one home per cycle, one layer per project

### Deliberation

The three changes are separable in principle and were kept together on purpose: rule 12's reframing
is what permits the `custom.md` split, and hard rule 13's land step is what finally gave the chores
backfill an owner. No single honest title covers all of it, which by our own hard rule 9 is evidence
of more than one step; the title above is a compromise and is recorded as such.

**What we got wrong first, twice.** The medium's commands live in `custom-family.md` now, so nine
pinned references naming `custom.md` looked stale and were repointed at a newly defined "project
layer". wink rejected it: an agent reads `custom.md`, meets a one-line directive, and follows it, so
a pinned file asking for something "in custom.md" is already answered. All nine were reverted to
byte-identical with the payload. The same instinct produced a `CLAUDE.md` that `@`-imported every
layer, which wink also rejected, on the ground that it makes `CLAUDE.md` a second statement of what
to read and therefore a second thing to keep true. Both mistakes were the same one: solving in the
pinned set what the project layer had already solved.

**The bookmark categories collide and it is unresolved.** `agent-files-model` has now hosted three
cycles without landing, which by the `jj.md` text written today makes it a long-lived bookmark
(merge-only, never rewritten) at the same time as a topic bookmark (a draft, freely rewritten). The
two are defined as mutually exclusive. Nothing forces a decision this commit, but the
`measure-reproducibility` rebase does, since it relies on the draft reading.

**Three rules this cycle breaks on its way in.** It has no opening commit, so hard rule 13 is
unobserved by the commit that introduces it. The close-out could not "run the acceptance check the
opening stated" because there was no opening. And the six provisional items have no defined home in
a single-commit cycle, since such a cycle skips `## In Progress` by the 2026-07-31 rule; they are in
this section by improvisation. The last one wants fixing in the text.

**vc-x1's contribution, and where we went past it.** Their tier-2 item #1 proposed ladder plus
narrative in one home; we made it six required items with `_None._` for an empty deliberation, and
folded their acceptance-check proposal in as the sixth. Their `chores-15` trial supplied the four
transforms of the move, the finding that two of them fail silently, and the measurement that anchors
survive the depth change because GitHub slugs derive from heading text rather than level. That last
one refuted an objection we had raised against using headings at all.

**Deferred.** `AGENTS.md` still says "the family" and "member" where the generic mechanism is "the
template payload and my copy of it", which is the same test that moved the family layer out of
`custom.md`, applied one level up. Left for its own cycle rather than doubling this one's review
surface.

content.text:
Fair — "layer" is doing work it never earned, and that is my fault twice over.

## What I meant, and why it is nebulous

By "layer" I meant *the project's own agent-files, as against the pinned ones*: `custom.md` plus
whatever it points at. The word comes from the loading order — it loads last and wins conflicts, so
it sits *over* the pinned set rather than beside it.

The problem is that nothing says so. `layer` currently appears in four places with no definition
anywhere:

- `AGENTS.md` hard rule 0, "the project's layer"
- `AGENTS.md`'s section heading, "custom.md: the project layer"
- `custom.md`'s own title, "the project layer"
- `custom-family.md`'s title, "iiac-perf's layer, as a member..."

And it is a gap I introduced. I *did* define it in Terminology a few turns ago, then reverted the
definition along with the nine repointed references when you rejected that approach. The references
went back; the term stayed. So you are reading a word that had a definition for about twenty minutes.

Contrast with **cycle**, which you can state exactly: three phases, one commit if single-step, two or
more if multi-step, `-0` foldable into `-1`, close-out bare. That is what a defined term looks like.

## Two fixes I would make

**1. Drop "layer" from the title.** It was carrying the second half of the change and cannot. The
honest unifying theme across all three parts is that each thing gets exactly one place: the bookmark
rules had no owner, `custom.md` held rules it did not own, and the chores record had two homes. So:

```
docs: one owner per rule, one home per record
```

and say "the project's own files", which costs four small edits and no new vocabulary.

```
docs: one owner per rule, one home per record

Two rules this project had agreed to were written down nowhere, and one
it had written down was wrong. Cycles had run on topic bookmarks for a
week on undocumented habit, with neither creating nor landing one
described in any agent-file. custom.md had drifted into holding rules
the family should own alongside facts that mean nothing outside it, so
it could not be handed to a project that had never heard of us. And the
chores record was specified to be built up per commit, which meant every
ladder rung written twice and every backfill applied in two files.

Every rule now sits in the file that owns it, and every record in one
place. A cycle runs on its own bookmark, created at the opening and
landed at the close-out, and landing is the beat that finally fires the
chores backfill. custom.md shrinks to a stub with nothing to substitute,
reaching everything of this project's own through a single line. A
cycle's record moves from the todo file into chores as a mechanical
step rather than a second authoring pass. Four of vc-x1's outstanding
items land alongside.
```

have not written anything yet.

35	### One warm loop, three policies
36	
37	The end state, decided 2026-08-01: one parameterized warm loop. Step the bench, probe
38	periodically, stop when the exit condition holds. The harness's three warms become policies over
39	that one mechanism:
40	
41	- the per-run warmup exits when the trailing window grades A, or at the cap
42	- the process warm (`process_warm`) exits on the `--settle-time` budget
43	- the block warm (`run_blocked`'s 2 ms spin) is the same loop with a fixed-time exit and probing

46	`process_warm` and `warmup_and_probe` already share one probe series, prober and time origin;
47	this completes the fusion instead of adding a fourth variant.
48	
49	Terminology: the warmup unit is a **warmup pass** (the 0.22.0-4 "loop-only passes" sense), a
50	short, unrecorded, timed burst of bench steps yielding one floor. Not a "probe": `TProbe` is the
51	measurement instrument, and the "micro-probe" is the 0.23.0 cycle's ~1 ms timer-pair frame
52	measurement.
53	
54	### The exit condition: grade the trailing window
55	
56	Rather than K agreeing floors, grade a *sliding window* over the warmup probe series and warm
57	until the trailing window reads A, or the cap (design 2026-07-28). The exit condition and the
58	warmup letter become one computation:
59	
60	- exit on A means the run started post-ramp by construction
61	- hitting the cap reports whatever the window actually scored, the "run started unstable" signal,
62	  not a silent proceed
63	- window length takes the same "minimum count or minimum wall time, whichever is larger" shape as
64	  pass length: count because the split detector needs 4 points a side, wall time because the ramp
65	  is a ms-scale phenomenon
66	- signals: spread, drift, step; `interference` is the weak one [[2]]
67	- the minimum wall span is load-bearing: a window can be far shorter than what it certifies
68	  (`min-now`'s 16 warmup probes span ~17 us against a transition arriving at ~800 ms), so
69	  agreement alone certifies nothing
70	
71	Floors, not means, so one preemption doesn't fake (in)stability; a warm box exits
72	near-immediately.
73	
74	Convergence is agreement, not direction. The 3900X is bistable (2026-07-27 `calibrate` runs):
75	sustained rapid repetition climbs it into a fast state (~0.445 ns/iter), low-duty isolated runs
76	sit at ~0.489 (B), ~9% apart, and transitions straddle windows in *both* directions; a fixed
77	warmup absorbs only transitions shorter than itself, whatever their sign.
78	
79	The hard cap sits at governor scale (a few hundred ms; exact constant measured on both boxes
80	during the rung). The cap doubles as the estimate-phase deadline the `--pin` guard Todo wants, so
81	slow and non-converging benches share one diagnostic exit.
82	
83	### Sizing fusion
84	
85	The warmup pass *is* the step-cost sizing pass: the converged floor is the sizing input, so
86	sizing is post-ramp by construction and convergence is tested on the number actually consumed.
87	The `estimate_step_cost` phase folds into the warm loop; the micro-probe supplies the frame
88	input, run after convergence.

91	whichever is larger) so a floor is never one sample. The cap exit then distinguishes "floors
92	disagreed" (unstable, gauge signal) from "too slow to certify" (proceed, label the run

version, a concise stamp that also gave the steps their order. A step
is one commit of a cycle. The problem is that a version can change at
any time, and preserving the order then forces a matching change
through every version after it.

effect on any other step. Order now comes from a rung's position in
its ladder. The one version still written down sits on a chores
as-built rung beside that commit's SHA, where it describes a landed
commit rather than naming a step.

- a Done entry is a bold title with sub-bullets
- a commit body is a problem statement plus a solution statement
- a topic bookmark is a draft, so its ladder stays self-consistent
  until it lands
- the dynamic warmup ladder is backfilled, eight rungs whose commits
  landed on main two cycles ago
- cycle.md now states the two cycle styles, single- and multi-step,

content.text:
The push refused cleanly — nothing committed, both repos untouched.

## What happened

`vc-x1 push` hard-errors on our legacy `.vc-config.toml` schema before running any stage. Both sides
were still `[workspace] path / other-repo` rather than `[repos] work / bot`.

**This corrects something I told you, and told vc-x1.** I had sampled `vc-x1 chid @` (exit 0) and
concluded "normal commands tolerate it". True of what I sampled, wrong as a generalisation — read,
log and diff accept the legacy schema; `push` does not. So a repo looks healthy for weeks and finds
out at the exact moment it tries to publish.

## Fixed

  size-per-se, and it points at the transport. It also means at least one member's environment
  silently changed behaviour on upgrade, which is worth a line somewhere even though the change was
  an improvement.

content.text:
Message updated. Three changes, one of which is new evidence for them.

## 1. It is no longer uncommitted

The opening said the configuration was "written and **uncommitted**", and the review command was
`jj diff -R ../iiac-perf ...`, which now shows nothing. Both replaced: the commit is `28e385d6`,
0.24.3, on `agent-files-model`, with `main` still at `3ab16586` so nothing is permanent. The review
command is now `jj show -R ../iiac-perf 28e385d6`.

I also added a third payload diff, `diff -u work/custom.md ../iiac-perf/custom.md`, with the note
that it should be a single line — which is a self-check on whether they have applied the stub
proposal, and the cleanest way to demonstrate the claim rather than assert it.

## 2. The sandbox push finding

This is the substantive one, and it partly reverses what the message said. It previously ended
"bugs.md #8's remaining mystery does not dissolve". It may have:

- This push **succeeded** from the sandboxed shell with a 3,029,662-byte bot-repo transcript.
- The 2026-08-06 failures died twice at ~3.4 MB — same sandbox, same https remotes, same box.
- The variable that changed is their binary: 0.71.0 shelled out to `git push`; 0.78.4 logged
  `squash-push-bot: ... (in-process)`.

Written as inference rather than measurement, since it is one success against two failures at a
slightly smaller size and I did not isolate the variable deliberately. The message says what would
settle it — one deliberate 0.71.0 push at ~3 MB from the same sandbox — and says we will not run it
unless they want it for #8's record, because it means reinstalling a binary with a known state bug
to confirm a diagnosis we no longer need.

## 3. Amendments are cheap until it lands

Added to the "Done when": the bookmark being unlanded is the point, so if they want changes we
rewrite and force-push rather than appending a fixup. Otherwise a reviewer reasonably assumes a
pushed commit is settled and softens their review.

## One follow-up I did not do

Our `permanently local` dogfood entry in `custom-family.md` still says pushes must run from your
shell. Its retirement condition is now met by a single data point. The message says we are leaving it
for one more push before retiring it, and I left the entry alone rather than editing it on one
observation — but it is stale enough that it should not sit for long.

## docs: the bot pushes again

- [[N]] docs: the bot pushes again

A single-commit cycle retiring a `permanently local` dogfood entry, per
[Retiring Done entries](../../agent-data/notes.md#retiring-done-entries): the narrative lands here
and the entry leaves `custom-family.md`, so that log carries in-flight entries only.

### Problem

Since 2026-08-06 every push has been handed to wink to run from his terminal, because `vc-x1 push`
from the bot's sandboxed shell died mid-transfer twice on a roughly 3.4 MB bot-repo push
(`send-pack: unexpected disconnect while reading sideband packet`). The workaround cost a round
trip on every cycle and the entry recording it has been wrong twice: first blaming ssh on a repo
whose remotes are and were https, then, once corrected, blaming nothing at all.

### Solution

The condition the entry named for its own retirement is met, so it retires and the bot pushes
directly again. The evidence and its limits move here, where a wrong cause in the record is a
historical note rather than a live instruction.

### Acceptance check

A push from the bot's sandboxed shell carrying a multi-MB bot-repo transfer completes. **This
cycle's own push is the check**, which is the whole reason it is a separate cycle rather than an
amendment to the one before it: a commit cannot contain evidence produced by its own push, and the
retirement rests on exactly that.

Result recorded at close-out. Two outcomes, both useful: success makes it two independent
observations rather than one, and failure un-retires the entry with better evidence than it had.

### Ladder

- [[N]] docs: the bot pushes again

### Deliberation

The measurement, 2026-08-07: pushing `docs: one owner per rule, one home per record` from the
sandbox succeeded, carrying a 3,029,662-byte transcript in the bot repo. Same sandbox, same box,
same https remotes as the failures. The log line read `squash-push-bot: ... (in-process)`.

**We think the subprocess git transport was the cause and the in-process jj-lib path fixed it.**
Marked as inference rather than measurement, and the limits stated because this entry has already
been wrong twice by not stating them: one success against two failures, 3.0 MB against 3.4 MB, and
the variable was not isolated deliberately. It changed because vc-x1 went from 0.71.0 to 0.78.4,
and the transport change came along with everything else in seven minor versions.

What would settle it is one deliberate 0.71.0 push at ~3 MB from the same sandbox. We are not
running it: it means reinstalling a binary with a known state bug to confirm a diagnosis we no
longer need. The offer stands to vc-x1 if they want it for bugs.md #8's record.

**Retiring on one data point is a judgement, not a certainty.** The alternative was to wait for a
second push, but that push would have had to carry something, and the only thing waiting to be
carried was this retirement. Making the retirement its own cycle resolves the circularity: the
check runs at the moment the record claims it passed.

**Bookmark note, still unresolved.** This is the fourth cycle on `agent-files-model` without a
landing, which by `jj.md` makes it a long-lived bookmark and a topic bookmark at once. Recorded
again rather than decided again; the `measure-reproducibility` rebase is what forces it.
